Abstract: Advances in monocular depth estimation (MDE) now let an attacker generate depth from publicly available RGB images and submit forged RGB-D queries. Such attacks break a core assumption of RGB-D place authentication: that depth comes from a sensor. We study a presentation attack detection (PAD) classifier that uses geometric consistency between the enrollment and query views, as a software-layer defense. A three-stage evaluation shows how far this classifier detects software-injected depth, depending on how accurately the attacker knows the camera intrinsics. In the first stage, the attacker has only an estimate of the intrinsics, and the PAD classifier separates forgeries generated by all three MDE models with a validation area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.997-0.999. In the second stage, the attacker obtains the exact intrinsics, and the original PAD classifier falls to near chance (AUC 0.54-0.61); a retrained PAD classifier, however, still has the registration residual between enrollment and query as a cue. In the third stage, an oracle evaluation, in which the evaluator fits warps using the ground-truth 3D geometry, shows that detection falls to near chance only in its strongest case, where every valid query keypoint is given its ground-truth 3D coordinate. Of the detection cues, the reprojection error captures the attacker's misestimate of the intrinsics, whereas the registration residual remains even when the attacker knows the exact intrinsics.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SCOUT: Planning under Occlusion via Object-Centric World Model Rollouts
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.01600v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Robots manipulating in cluttered spaces must often plan from partial views where foreground objects occlude the target, surrounding geometry, and usable free space. Reactive policies often miss these hidden constraints, while exhaustive search becomes computationally prohibitive in dense clutter. We present SCOUT, an occlusion-aware planning framework that bridges high-level deliberation with grounded physical rollouts. SCOUT leverages an object-centric scene representation to reconstruct hidden geometry and derive a relational planning state capturing blocker hierarchies and accessibility corridors. To navigate the vast action space in clutter, an LLM proposes structured action candidates which are then rigorously evaluated via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) using a learned action-conditioned world model. Evaluations on 'Reveal' and 'Placement' tasks show that SCOUT outperforms Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, embodied agents, and 3D world models, with significant gains in long-horizon tasks requiring reasoning over occluded geometry. We further validate the framework's robustness through real-world robotic manipulation in a cluttered shelf environment.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: LLM-Enhanced Multimodal House Price Prediction using Structured, Textual, and Visual Features
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.01615v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Accurate house price prediction is essential for real estate buyers, sellers, agents, and financial institutions. Traditional methods rely primarily on structured data, e.g., number of bedrooms, bathrooms, parkings, but they overlook rich contextual information embedded in textual descriptions and property photos. Previous deep learning approaches for house price prediction have fused multimodal data but they fall short to extract structured spatio-temporal and contextual features from texts and semantic visual information from images. In this paper, we introduce a novel multimodal framework that addresses these limitations by systematically integrating structured attributes, textual descriptions, and visual images of properties to achieve higher prediction accuracy while maintaining interpretability. We use a large language model to derive domain-specific spatio-temporal and contextual features from text, and an unsupervised vision-language approach to automatically group photos into meaningful classes like indoor, outdoor, mixed, or floorplan, that are commonly present in real-world house listings. These categories are created without manual labeling by aligning image clusters with carefully designed pseudo text prompts. We fuse all features into a unified representation and use an optimized regressor to predict prices. Experiments on a large real-world property dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms traditional methods and existing multimodal baselines. Ablation studies confirm that the novel textual feature extraction and categorized visual embeddings substantially contribute to more accurate and reliable price predictions.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Seeing What Matters, Verifying What Pays: Load-Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.01617v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates vision-language model (VLM) inference without altering the output distribution, yet two factors limit its gains. Existing drafters either lack the image evidence required for visually grounded tokens or pay to condition on every visual token, although a short draft block typically depends on only a few image regions. Moreover, the value of verifying additional candidates varies with GPU load, so no fixed verification structure is efficient across serving conditions. We present Uni-LaSpec, a block-parallel speculative decoding framework that addresses both factors. To improve draft quality, Uni-LaSpec reuses the verifier's own attention: the query retained from the preceding verification ranks the cached, int8-quantized visual keys, and a cross-layer vote selects a few visual tokens that the drafter fuses through gated cross-attention. Acceptance-aware training further weights each draft position by its contribution to the accepted prefix. To allocate verification, a marginal-cost criterion selects the structure per request and per round: draft trees exploit idle verifier capacity under light load, whereas a dynamic head truncates linear drafts under heavy load. Across six VLMs from three model families and 17 text and multimodal benchmarks, selecting eight visual tokens retains at least 98.6% of the acceptance obtained from the full image at sub-millisecond selection cost. With greedy decoding at concurrency one, Uni-LaSpec achieves up to 5.11x text and 3.24x multimodal throughput over autoregressive decoding. Across six load levels and three GPU types, it outperforms autoregressive decoding in every setting and matches or exceeds the best fixed verification strategy in 123 of 144 settings; under bursty arrivals, it reduces mean end-to-end latency by 47.6% relative to linear verification.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Learned optical compression for single-pixel quantitative phase imaging
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.01675v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) reveals optical path-length variations in transparent objects but typically relies on spatially resolved intensity measurements. Here we numerically and experimentally demonstrate learned optical compression for single-pixel QPI, jointly optimizing a diffractive encoder and a digital neural decoder to concentrate reconstruction-relevant phase information into a compact measurement vector. A single reconfigurable phase-modulation plane sequentially displays the learned encoding patterns, which are independent of the input object, each yielding one scalar intensity measurement. Operating at a visible wavelength, the experimental system reconstructs quantitative phase images of unknown objects with ~40-fold dimensional compression, using only 2.55% as many intensity measurements as reconstructed pixels. Experimental blind testing on handwritten digits and grating-like phase objects achieves mean Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.945 and 0.848, respectively. Benchmarking under the same measurement budget demonstrates substantially higher reconstruction fidelity than other encoding strategies, highlighting the advantages of learned optical compression. With the optical encoder fixed, decoder-only neural adaptation enables experimental transfer to previously unseen data distributions, extending the utility of the learned measurement representation. These results establish learned optical compression as a measurement-efficient and reusable framework for QPI, integrating phase-information compression into single-pixel intensity measurements while retaining adaptability to new data. This approach paves the way for low-data-rate phase imaging and sensing, with the potential to extend QPI to spectral regions where high-quality detector arrays are costly or unavailable.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: TriPhysBench: Evaluating Physical Intelligence for Embodied Agents
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.01934v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Embodied agents need physical intelligence to understand their surroundings through physical perception, physical knowledge retrieval, and physical reasoning. These capabilities must work together to interpret events and make quantitative judgments. Existing benchmarks advance physical understanding and general-purpose tool use, yet the coordination of these capabilities in physical scenarios remains insufficiently characterized. Inspired by Popper's Three Worlds, we introduce TriPhysBench, a benchmark of 410 questions from 200 videos that brings physical perception, physical knowledge retrieval, and physical reasoning into a shared evaluation setting. Its measurement-grounded and knowledge-grounded subtasks impose complementary demands on obtaining observations and acquiring external specifications, then applying them to quantitative problems. Among six representative vision-language models, the best achieves an answer accuracy of only 50.38%, revealing limited performance on tasks that require these capabilities to work together. We further introduce TriPhys, a framework that learns a unified policy for physical perception, knowledge retrieval, and quantitative reasoning from complete tool-integrated trajectories. The policy uses intermediate reasoning to guide retrieval and computation, then incorporates tool feedback into subsequent physical inference. On 110 questions from videos excluded from training, TriPhys improves answer and solution scores across three Qwen configurations, with a 17.7% relative gain in answer accuracy for TriPhys-27B over its Qwen3.6-27B backbone. This work provides a benchmark and a learning pathway toward embodied agents that move beyond recognizing events to understanding and reasoning about the physical processes behind them.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Answering Without Arriving: An Evidence Audit for Embodied Question Answering
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.01958v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Embodied question answering asks an agent to navigate, observe, and then answer questions about what it saw, yet answer accuracy alone cannot tell whether any of this happened. A plausible answer can come from the question, the room label, or the answer choices, and a correct answer does not show that the supporting observation was ever made. We present a multi-room benchmark whose 200 test episodes and 800 questions are stratified by route extent, with an evaluation ladder that holds the questions fixed while varying only the evidence supplied to the answerer, from text-only probes through closed-loop agents to replay of the reference trajectory. Questions are generated from symbolic records of rooms, visible objects, and frames, so every answer can be traced to the observations that support it. A closed-loop vision-language agent reaches no target in 200 episodes yet answers 45.5% of questions, within 0.1 points of the same model given no images; replaying the reference trajectory raises the same model to 57.4%, so the evidence exists along the route but is not gathered. A family-level audit then shows that access to evidence is not the same as use of it. Four of eight families are largely answerable from text, one cites frames that cannot establish its own answer, and the oracle conditions reach 59.5% on Rooms-visited by counting the supplied images. Evidence acquisition, answer coverage, and shortcut sensitivity must therefore be established before an accuracy gain can be credited to memory.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Cross-Dataset Generalization of Glaucoma Detection CNNs: Effects of Operating Threshold, Multi-Source Training, and Color Normalization
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.01992v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Deep learning models for glaucoma detection are usually tested on images from the same dataset used for training. That says little about how they will work at a new hospital or with a new camera. We fine-tuned five ImageNet-pretrained CNNs (ResNet50, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0, InceptionV3) with identical settings on one of three public fundus datasets (ACRIMA, ORIGA, RIM-ONE DL). Each was tested on a held-out part of its own dataset and on the other two datasets in full. We used three random seeds and report mean and SD over seeds. Mean in-domain AUC was 0.913 and cross-source AUC was 0.702, a drop of 0.211 (SD 0.030; 95% CI 0.135 to 0.286). After correction for multiple comparisons we found no evidence that any architecture did better, though three seeds give low power. At thresholds set on the source validation data, specificity fell from 0.870 to 0.506 and sensitivity from 0.831 to 0.726. Resetting the threshold on 10% of the target images raised specificity to 0.670 but lowered sensitivity to 0.609, and balanced accuracy rose only from 0.616 to 0.639. Training on two sources together did not help (held-out AUC 0.695 versus 0.702). LAB reference normalization (cross-source AUC 0.755) and strong color augmentation (0.754) gave similar gains, cutting the drop to about 0.16. Ben Graham normalization (0.733) and CLAHE (0.712) helped less, and gray-world (0.696) did not help. The two best methods raised specificity but lowered sensitivity. On G1020, used only for testing, AUC stayed near 0.5 in every condition, and networks trained within G1020 were also close to chance. Strong in-domain results do not show that a glaucoma model will work on new data. Normalization and color augmentation reduce the drop but do not remove it. Studies should report external validation and check the operating threshold, not only AUC.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Scalar Smoothness Is One Point on a Besov Spectrum
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.02037v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Studies of neural network generalization and robustness often summarize smoothness with a single number, such as a Lipschitz constant or a Hessian curvature statistic. However, Lipschitz constants summarize global worst-case sensitivity and Hessian statistics summarize local curvature; neither captures how model responses vary with the size, direction, and location of perturbations encountered in real-world deployment. To measure smoothness under these perturbations, we introduce a finite-difference roughness spectrum that profiles model responses across these conditions. Our roughness spectrum generalizes scalar smoothness measures, bringing Lipschitz sensitivity and directional Hessian curvature into a common framework across perturbation scales. We connect this spectrum to classical Besov theory, which describes how a function's variation changes with scale. Our theoretical analysis also proves that a larger output shift can cause less task damage than a smaller one, and that local curvature alone can miss the blocks most vulnerable to finite perturbations. In image classification, Roughness Source Control (RSC) suppresses margin roughness along noise directions and improves noise robustness in a comparison of 80 checkpoints across four model--dataset combinations. In post-training quantization, we identify blocks that need higher precision by measuring task-loss increases from perturbations matched to the size and direction of each block's quantization error. Our mixed-precision allocation achieves lower perplexity than the Hessian-based HAWQ-V2 baseline under the same GPTQ weights and bit budgets in all 14 settings across seven held-out large language models.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Do Embodied VLMs Actually Use Their Scene-Graph Memory?
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.02056v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Embodied agents that answer questions about their route need a memory of what they saw, and scene graphs are a natural form for it. A vision-language model (VLM) can receive such a graph as text or through a graph encoder, but accuracy alone cannot show whether the graph holds the episode's facts, reaches the model, or is actually relied on. In this diagnostic study, we introduce a graph-swap test for the last of these: each episode is given another episode's graph, and we count how many answers change. On an embodied question-answering benchmark with routes through two to seven rooms, we use it to compare ways of delivering scene-graph memory to a fine-tuned VLM. As text, the memory is used strongly, adding 30 points on route questions. As a graph, it is not, and we trace why: the encoder preserves the information, but standard pooled and late fusion discard it. Giving each node its own input token recovers part of it, a gain of 8.3 points on route questions that the swap test confirms comes from the graph. The test also exposes a shortcut that accuracy hides: when the same facts appear in the text, the model ignores its graph. The test thus offers a cheap check of whether a VLM uses its scene-graph memory, and our analysis points to how that memory should be delivered.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: When Delay Meets Drift: Physical Safety of Robot Foundation Models Is a Cross-Layer Problem
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.02101v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Robot foundation models now act in a closed loop, yet their safety is evaluated one variation at a time: robustness benchmarks perturb the scene while assuming instantaneous inference, and real-time execution methods study inference delay in nominal scenes. We argue that physical safety is not a property of the model alone, but emerges from how variations in the physical environment, the model, the computing platform, and execution interact in closed loop. We formalize this as cross-layer variation propagation across these system layers and use an interaction contrast to measure when joint variation creates more risk than the sum of its parts. In 4,000 paired closed-loop episodes of the pi0.5 vision-language-action model on LIBERO, a 400 ms inference delay raises the safety-violation rate by 3.5 percentage points under the training viewpoint but by 37 percentage points under a 60-degree camera shift: 33.5 percentage points (95% CI: 25-43) more than the two effects combined. We close with a research agenda toward predictable physical intelligence: predicting when variation becomes risk, and adapting compute, power, and control accordingly.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Modeling Visual Cortex with Layerwise Multiscale Manifold Capacity Maximization
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.02245v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Task-optimized deep neural networks have risen to prominence as the most predictive phenomenological models of responses in primate visual cortex, but leave much to be desired from the perspective of biological plausibility. One such limitation is the reliance on precise credit assignment through global backpropagation of error signals. Recent work has shown that this weakness can be circumvented by requiring each subsequent stage to solve a distinct and increasingly complex task, allowing for layerwise local learning signals. We propose a novel strategy for crafting such intermediate losses that uses an efficient coding framework formulated in terms of manifold capacity, and which can be computed using a sequence of {canonical cortical computations}. In particular, we leverage the relationship between the multiscale nature of visual signals and the dilation of receptive field sizes in cascaded visual representations to modulate complexity, allowing for the reapplication of these common loss computations at each stage of the hierarchy. We evaluate our approach on its ability to predict neural datasets spanning three areas of the ventral stream hierarchy in macaques, as well as human psychophysical data on an object classification task. We find that our unsupervised layerwise model matches or exceeds the performance of competitive architecture-matched baselines on all evaluations considered.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Spectral-spatial vision test-time training for hyperspectral image classification
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.02364v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification requires the representation of contiguous spectral signatures and spatial context under limited labeled supervision. Vision test-time training (TTT) offers an alternative to fixed-weight token mixing by performing self-supervised inner-model updates on the input sequence, but its application to center-pixel HSI classification remains insufficiently characterized. We present ViTTT-HSI, a spectral-spatial adaptation of the vision test-time training (ViT3) architecture. A spectral-aware embedding stem extracts ordered-band information using spectral convolution and forms spatial tokens without reducing their spatial resolution. Two ViT3-based TTT encoder blocks perform patch-conditioned token mixing, followed by the fusion of center-pixel and neighborhood-average features for classification. We evaluate the framework on Indian Pines, Pavia University, Salinas, and Houston 2013 using ten random seeds and dataset-specific training fractions of 1% or 5%. The mean overall accuracies are 97.6390%, 98.8753%, 99.3292%, and 98.4283%, respectively. Ablations reveal a substantial contribution from the TTT inner update on Indian Pines and a smaller positive contribution on Pavia University, while the relative benefits of the spectral stem and feature fusion depend on the dataset. The results demonstrate the feasibility of using patch-conditioned vision TTT for spectral--spatial HSI classification and highlight the role of the inner adaptation mechanism.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Do Visual RL Gains Scale at Test Time? A Quantile View of Post-Training
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.02366v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves the single-sample quality of visual generative models, but deployment often provides additional inference compute through Best-of-N sampling. Whether RL gains transfer under such test-time scaling, particularly on difficult held-out tasks, remains poorly understood in the visual domain. Our central contribution is to systematically identify and characterize a failure mode of scaling transfer in visual RL: across multiple RL methods, model backbones, and evaluations spanning compositional generation, text rendering, and preference alignment, higher single-sample reward does not necessarily imply a better quality-compute frontier. RL gains may attenuate, saturate, or even reverse at large sampling budgets, with the base model eventually outperforming its post-trained counterpart. We explain these regimes through a quantile-transfer framework, showing that Best-of-N places increasing weight on the upper tail of the reward distribution as N grows. Consequently, RL can improve typical samples while compressing or degrading the rare high-quality outcomes that test-time scaling exploits. As a simple intervention motivated by this analysis, we introduce Quantile Utility Policy Optimization (QUPO), which optimizes a controllable mixture of quantile utilities corresponding to different inference budgets. Experiments on SD3.5-M and BAGEL show that QUPO better preserves upper-tail quality and substantially improves scaling on challenging held-out prompts relative to standard RL post-training. Our results suggest that visual generative models should be evaluated and optimized not only for single-sample quality, but for how post-training reshapes the full reward distribution that inference-time scaling exploits.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MirrorComm: A Communication-Efficient Cooperative Perception Framework via Mirrored World Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.02405v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Cooperative perception (CP) requires substantial communication bandwidth to exchange sensing information among connected agents. A variety of compression techniques have been proposed to reduce transmission costs while retaining task-relevant information. However, most existing methods follow a frame-wise compression paradigm, overlooking temporal predictability and repeatedly transmitting information that could be inferred from historical context. To address these limitations, we propose MirrorComm, the first world model-based communication-efficient CP framework. Specifically, mirrored world models at the transmitter and receiver predict the transmitter's current observation from a shared history of its reconstructed observations. The transmitter compares this prediction with its current observation and selectively transmits observation updates to correct prediction errors, reducing repeated transmission of predictable information. Experiments on the OPV2V dataset across two downstream tasks including object detection and semantic segmentation show that MirrorComm reduces communication bandwidth requirements by up to approximately 66-fold while maintaining comparable performance to a state-of-the-art (SOTA) method. Ablation studies further demonstrate the effectiveness of the individual components.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: End-to-End Stability of Online Active Learning in Large-Scale Neural Systems
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.02488v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Online Active Learning (OAL) aims to extend deep learning from static inference after offline training to continuous adaptation during real-time interaction with a changing physical environment. This transition is essential for safety-critical applications, but it raises a central theoretical question: whether the online parameter update process remains stable when scaled to multilayer neural architectures. This paper develops a stability-focused OAL framework. The framework uses prediction error as a feedback signal to update a structured deep model, thereby linking online learning with Lyapunov-based energy minimization. We show that prediction error convergence alone is insufficient for global parameter convergence because multilayer networks may admit high-dimensional manifolds of equivalent output solutions. The analysis therefore separates output error regulation, internal zero dynamics, interlayer coupling, and parameter convergence. Persistency of excitation and active damping are then used to remove the residual null-space modes that remain after output error convergence. A cascaded Lyapunov analysis establishes asymptotic stability of the overall OAL learning process, while monotonic activation functions and diffeomorphic layer mappings provide the uniqueness condition for the target parameter trajectory. The resulting proof provides a theoretical basis for applying online adaptive learning to large-scale neural systems in nonstationary and safety-critical settings.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Probing Local Conditional Fit for Diffusion Model Membership Inference
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.02578v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Membership inference determines whether a candidate example was used to train a text-to-image diffusion model and is an important tool for auditing training-data use. We identify a directional membership signal in \emph{conditional prediction shifts}, the changes in predicted noise under alternative text conditions at a fixed noisy input: whether movement toward the alternative prediction initially lowers or raises the denoising loss from its value under the original caption. Members exhibit less room for such local improvement. To quantify this response, we propose \emph{LoFIT} (Local Conditional Fit), which measures the initial response of the denoising loss along normalized prediction shifts and aggregates it across multiple text conditions and diffusion states. LoFIT requires no target-model gradients and can be computed using only forward queries to the denoiser. Evaluations on four datasets show improved membership discrimination across fine-tuned and pretrained models. LoFIT distinguishes members early in fine-tuning, while the naive denoising-loss baseline remains near chance. Controlled comparisons show that the membership signal is concentrated in the first-order response, with little discrimination from prediction-shift magnitude alone.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Camera-Free Object Discovery and Interaction with GazeTags
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.02599v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We present GazeTags, a camera- and computer-vision-free approach for worn head-gaze object awareness. Our small electronic tags cost roughly \$2 each and can operate for more than a year on a coin cell battery. They work in concert with a user-worn device (smartglasses, hearables, etc.) that periodically emits a focused infrared signal aligned with the user's head direction. Only GazeTags within that narrow head-oriented beam wake and respond, providing their identity and optional payloads such as object state or live sensor readings. By avoiding cameras and computer vision pipelines, our approach is very energy efficient, able to operate continuously even in battery-constrained wearables, and sidesteps non-trivial privacy issues. We describe our hardware design, characterize our system performance and operating tradeoffs, and demonstrate how GazeTags can enable practical gaze-aware environments.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Parametric CAD Bench v3: Evaluating Agentic Parametric CAD Authoring from Text and Engineering Drawings
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.02659v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Producing an executable CAD script is not sufficient to establish that an agent has satisfied an engineering design request. Evaluation must also consider the resulting geometry, specified dimensions, and native CAD modeling history. We present Parametric CAD Bench v3, a 100-task benchmark comprising 30 text-to-CAD creation tasks, 30 text-to-CAD create-and-edit tasks, and 40 tasks that reconstruct mechanical parts from engineering drawings. Agents operate in a pinned FreeCAD environment and submit native CAD artifacts to a separate programmatic verifier. The primary metric is mean continuous task reward, combining geometry similarity and specification consistency rather than binary task success. A September 24, 2026 snapshot covers 13 model-agent systems; Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 achieves the highest overall point estimate, 61.03%, and an image-to-CAD mean reward of 84.66%. These measurements describe complete systems, not isolated model capabilities. We release versioned tasks, evaluation configurations, and inspectable result artifacts.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Human-Oriented World Model
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.02690v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Supporting a person over repeated interactions requires interpreting their current state in context and anticipating its subsequent evolution. We formulate the \emph{Human-Oriented World Model} (HOWM) as a conceptual framework centered on task-relevant human states and their evolution. HOWM connects current observations and individual history with environmental and social context to organize continuing state estimation, personalized dynamics prediction, and action support. Dynamic expectations and new observations jointly inform the current estimate, which in turn anchors personalized forecasts based on shared knowledge and individual experience. An external policy relates forecasts under alternative conditions to the person's goals, preferences, and constraints when considering support. Actual responses and outcomes provide evidence for revising the state estimate and personal dynamic patterns, thereby informing subsequent estimation, prediction, and support. We illustrate the framework through hypothetical training and learning scenarios. Our research agenda asks whether accumulated interaction experience improves subsequent estimation and prediction, and whether using the model helps the person pursue their goals over time.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: LipLingo: CNN Model for Lip Reading
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.02776v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Lip reading plays a crucial role in applications such as speech recognition, assistive technologies for the hearing-impaired, and biometric authentication. However, performance often degrades when the speaker varies and when certain speech sounds are visually similar. To address these challenges, we propose LipLingo, a robust lip-reading system based on the LipNet architecture, enhanced with a standardized preprocessing pipeline for consistent mouth-region representation, a rotational validation strategy for improved generalization to unseen speakers, and a flexible similarity evaluation for more reliable sentence-level assessment. The model architecture combines 3D convolutional layers for spatio-temporal feature extraction and bidirectional recurrent layers for sequence modeling, optimized using the Adam optimizer and Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) loss. On the GRID dataset, LipLingo achieved 95.0\% character-level accuracy (CER 4.99\%) and 87.2\% sentence-level accuracy. At the corpus level, the system obtained a (WER 13.1\%), outperforming the baseline LipNet and demonstrating competitive performance relative to recent 3D-ResNet + Bi-GRU + MixUp approaches. These results provide insights into strategies that enhance lip-reading robustness and highlight directions for future work toward real-world deployment.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: PlanContext: Benchmarking In-Context Driving Decision-Making
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.03067v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Real-world driving requires context-aware decision-making. Existing end-to-end driving benchmarks primarily assess trajectory quality through safety, compliance, comfort, and driving progress, leaving context-dependent decision-making insufficiently characterized. To fill this gap, we present PlanContext, a benchmark for evaluating in-context driving decision-making. PlanContext constructs paired evaluations by varying high-level driving intentions while keeping the observed scene fixed, enabling a natural and controllable assessment of context-dependent decision-making. We further define six representative driving contexts and jointly evaluate contextual decision correctness, road compliance, and dynamic safety with class-balanced metrics. Experiments on 9,561 scene-condition instances from NAVSIM and 23 public end-to-end driving models show that high conventional driving-quality scores do not consistently correspond to strong route-level in-context driving decision-making. Further analysis shows that model behavior varies with decision timing, road structure, and traffic interaction depending on the decision required by the current context. Our results highlight in-context driving decision-making as an important complementary dimension for evaluating end-to-end driving systems.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Shared-Pattern Collaborative Network for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Data Classification
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.03069v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Multi-source remote sensing data classification has received growing attention recently. However, existing methods still struggle to jointly model long-range contextual dependencies and shared spatial patterns across heterogeneous modalities. To address this issue, we propose a Shared-Pattern Collaborative Network (SPCNet) for HSI and SAR/LiDAR joint classification. To enhance cross-modal collaborative learning, Shared-Pattern Collaborative Block (SPCB) is designed by introducing a shared large-kernel operator and a dynamic convolution branch, enabling the network to capture common spatial structures and content-adaptive local features. Furthermore, Region-Adaptive Modality Allocator (RAMA) is developed to assign spatially varying modality weights for reliable feature fusion. Experiments on Houston2013, Augsburg, and Houston2018 datasets demonstrate that SPCNet achieves superior classification performance over several state-of-the-art methods. The code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/oucailab/SPCNet

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Cross-Layer Refinement and Frequency-aware Fusion Network for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Image Classification
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.03078v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Multi-source remote sensing image classification benefits from complementary spectral and structural information. However, identifying discriminative cross-modal features remains challenging. This letter proposes a Cross-Layer Refinement and Frequency-aware Fusion Network (CRFNet) within a lightweight dual-branch architecture. Specifically, a Cross-Layer Refinement Attention (CLRA) module propagates selected attention relationships across successive layers and employs top relation selection to progressively strengthen discriminative spatial dependencies while suppressing irrelevant responses. Furthermore, a Frequency-aware Complementary Fusion (FCF) module combines frequency-wise interactions with cross-modal channel attention in the Fourier domain. The resulting representations are then converted into spatial-domain gates to selectively modulate complementary features. Experiments on the Houston 2013 and Augsburg datasets demonstrate that the proposed CRFNet consistently outperforms several state-of-the-art methods. The codes are publicly available at https://github.com/oucailab/CRFNet

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Same Outputs, Different Scores: Auditing the Unchecked Graders of Multimodal LLM Benchmarks
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.03377v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Every multimodal-LLM multiple-choice benchmark ends with a scoring rule that converts a model's response, often free-form text rather than a clean option letter, into a right/wrong verdict, buried in its code. Unlike the dataset, this rule is chosen without justification and left unexamined, yet it sets the published number. We reproduce the official scorers of eight peer-reviewed benchmarks on five open vision-language models (VLMs) that fit a single 16 GB GPU, and introduce a blinded human-plus-LLM-judge adjudication (Cohen's kappa=0.956) that recovers what the model actually answered. The scoring rule alone moves accuracy by up to 22 points on identical outputs, yet exactly 0 wherever a model emits clean option letters, so it hides on strong-model leaderboards. It is the fallback and not the rambling that does the damage: the benchmark with the highest non-compliance we measure has an artifact of exactly zero, because its scorer abstains instead of guessing; a reasoning model with non-compliance 0.000 still swings 9.5 points with which regex match of its trace the parser keeps. No standard rule is reliable: snapping a non-answer to its closest option credits answers never given yet buries correct ones, abstention discards answers stated in words, and likelihood scoring follows answer-token priors, so a single grade conflates capability with luck rather than measuring either. We release all code, labels, and the protocol, and argue benchmarks should report a non-compliance rate and at least two rules, not one unexamined grade.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Comments: Accepted at WACV 2027 (Evaluations and Datasets Track). Code and data: this https URL

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: HIVE-Diff: High Frame Rate HDR Video Reconstruction from a Single LDR Frame and Events
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.03465v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: High frame rate HDR video is important in applications such as autonomous driving and scientific imaging, where rapid motion and extreme illumination often occur simultaneously. Conventional frame cameras face a trade-off between temporal resolution and dynamic range, while event cameras provide complementary high-speed brightness-change measurements over a wide illumination range. These properties have motivated event-based HDR reconstruction, with existing methods broadly following event-only and hybrid event-frame paradigms. Event-only HDR reconstruction, however, suffers from brightness and color drift due to the lack of absolute intensity references. Hybrid event-frame methods alleviate this ambiguity using low-dynamic-range (LDR) frames as anchors, but most perform one-to-one HDR reconstruction at available LDR timestamps. In this work, we investigate single-reference HDR temporal expansion, reconstructing N HDR frames from one LDR reference and events instead of N aligned LDR observations. We develop HIVE-Diff, an event-conditioned video diffusion framework that decomposes the task into event-guided temporal generation and HDR content completion. Because paired real HDR-event data are scarce, we train on synthetic data and adapt the model to real event domains using LDR-event sequences as proxy supervision with teacher-student distillation. Experiments on synthetic and multiple real-world datasets demonstrate strong reconstruction quality and robust real-data adaptation.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Comments: Accepted to WACV 2027 (Applications Track). 8 pages main paper + 8 pages supplementary material (included as appendix), 12 figures, 5 tables. Code: this https URL

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.03647v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Sensorized human demonstrations offer scalable data for mobile manipulation, but embodiment differences complicate policy learning. We present Pixel-UMI, a pipeline for learning environment-aware whole-body policies from human data. We first introduce Environment-Aware Retargeting (EAR), which combines reconstructed scene geometry with demonstrated head and gripper trajectories to determine robot posture and generate collision-aware joint and base targets. Delay-calibrated action assignment converts these trajectories into actions. However, kinematic differences can leave residual pose errors, creating viewpoint mismatches between human demonstrations and robot observations. We therefore introduce Retargeting-Error-Aware Masking (REAM), which uses these errors during training to reduce reliance on mismatched views at deployment. Finally, because estimated actions cannot fully capture contact-rich interactions, we collect on-policy human corrections through DAgger to improve performance. We evaluate Pixel-UMI on five challenging tasks spanning articulated-object manipulation, deformable-object handling, constrained-space reaching, whole-body collision avoidance, and contact-rich bimanual coordination, achieving 87.0% average task progress. Video results are available at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel-umi

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2611.03648v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: General-purpose mobile manipulation requires a combination of capable robot hardware, scalable demonstration collection, expressive whole-body control, and effective policy learning. Yet these components are often developed independently, creating mismatches that limit the capabilities of the complete system. We present Pixel, a co-designed full-stack system for learning general-purpose mobile manipulation. Pixel combines a low-cost wheeled humanoid with human-aligned kinematics and compliant grippers, multiple teleoperation and robot-free human data-collection interfaces, a unified whole-body controller, and a common policy learning pipeline across human and robot demonstrations. A hierarchical learning stack further enables language-conditioned visuomotor control and long-horizon task execution. We evaluate the system across hardware, data collection, and policy learning, and demonstrate mobile-manipulation behaviors requiring dexterity, active perception, navigation, and whole-body coordination. We hope that Pixel provides an integrated and extensible foundation for studying how robot hardware, data, control, and learning can be designed together for robot learning. More results at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MindEye2: Shared-Subject Models Enable fMRI-To-Image With 1 Hour of Data
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2403.11207v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Reconstructions of visual perception from brain activity have improved tremendously, but the practical utility of such methods has been limited. This is because such models are trained independently per subject where each subject requires dozens of hours of expensive fMRI training data to attain high-quality results. The present work showcases high-quality reconstructions using only 1 hour of fMRI training data. We pretrain our model across 7 subjects and then fine-tune on minimal data from a new subject. Our novel functional alignment procedure linearly maps all brain data to a shared-subject latent space, followed by a shared non-linear mapping to CLIP image space. We then map from CLIP space to pixel space by fine-tuning Stable Diffusion XL to accept CLIP latents as inputs instead of text. This approach improves out-of-subject generalization with limited training data and also attains state-of-the-art image retrieval and reconstruction metrics compared to single-subject approaches. MindEye2 demonstrates how accurate reconstructions of perception are possible from a single visit to the MRI facility. All code is available on GitHub.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Relational Representation Learning Network for Cross-Spectral Image Patch Matching
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2403.11751v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Recently, feature relation learning has drawn widespread attention in cross-spectral image patch matching. However, existing related research focuses on capturing diverse feature relations between image patches and ignores sufficient intrinsic feature representations of individual image patches. To address this limitation, we propose an innovative relational representation learning that simultaneously focuses on sufficiently mining the intrinsic features of individual image patches and the feature relations between image patches. Based on this, we construct a Relational Representation Learning Network (RRL-Net). Specifically, we innovatively construct an autoencoder to effectively characterize the individual intrinsic features, and introduce a feature interaction learning (FIL) module to extract deep-level feature relations. Meanwhile, to further fully mine individual intrinsic features, a lightweight multi-dimensional global-to-local attention (MGLA) module is constructed to enhance the global feature extraction of individual image patches and capture local dependencies within global features. By combining the MGLA module, we further explore the feature extraction network and construct an attention-based lightweight feature extraction (ALFE) network. Furthermore, a multi-loss post-pruning (MLPP) optimization strategy is proposed, which can greatly facilitate network optimization while avoiding increases in parameters and inference time. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our RRL-Net achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on multiple public datasets. Our code is available at https://github.com/YuChuang1205/RRL-Net

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Bukva: Russian Sign Language Alphabet
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2410.08675v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: This paper investigates the recognition of the Russian fingerspelling alphabet, also known as the Russian Sign Language (RSL) dactyl. Dactyl is a component of sign languages where distinct hand movements represent individual letters of a written language. This method is used to spell words without specific signs, such as proper nouns or technical terms. The alphabet learning simulator is an essential isolated dactyl recognition application. There is a notable issue of data shortage in isolated dactyl recognition: existing Russian dactyl datasets lack subject heterogeneity, contain insufficient samples, or cover only static signs. We provide Bukva, the first full-fledged open-source video dataset for RSL dactyl recognition. It contains 3,757 videos with more than 101 samples for each RSL alphabet sign, including dynamic ones. We utilized crowdsourcing platforms to increase the subject's heterogeneity, resulting in the participation of 155 deaf and hard-of-hearing experts in the dataset creation. We use a TSM (Temporal Shift Module) block to handle static and dynamic signs effectively, achieving 83.6% top-1 accuracy with a real-time inference with CPU only. The dataset, demo code, and pre-trained models are publicly available.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Smart Surveillance: Deep Learning and Hybrid Approaches for Dynamic Scene Analysis, Object Detection and Motion Tracking
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2412.05331v5 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Event-triggered recording reduces the footage a surveillance camera must store, but the trigger decides how much idle video is kept, how many events are missed, and how much computation is spent. We compare six motion triggers (frame differencing, dense optical flow, MOG2, KNN, CNT, GSOC), a CNN detector, strided detection, and three motion-gated hybrids under one recording policy, on a benchmark of seven static-camera scenes (5,800 frames, 27 annotated events) with thresholds transferred to unseen scenes by leave-one-video-out. Detector-based triggers stored 19-28% of idle frames, against 36-89% for motion triggers. Under simulated camera jitter, frame differencing, optical flow, MOG2 and KNN stored 97-100% of idle frames, while detector triggers stayed below 29%. Running the detector on every 8th frame kept 99.7% of event frames at 9.8 ms of CPU per frame, cheaper and more robust than gating it with background subtraction. On VisDrone, raising YOLO11n's input from 640 to 1280 px raised AP from 15.5 to 26.8, more than a larger model, and INT8 quantization cut latency by 17% for 0.3 AP. In tracking, longer track memory raised IDF1 from 70.5 to 76.7, but every tracker recovered only 39-44% of overlapped people, because detection rather than association failed.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Why and How: Knowledge-Guided Learning for Cross-Spectral Image Patch Matching
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2412.11161v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Recently, cross-spectral image patch matching based on feature relation learning has attracted extensive attention. However, existing methods focus on mining richer feature relations by building complex relation extraction structures. Meanwhile, performance bottlenecks have gradually emerged. To address this, we make the first attempt to explore a stable and efficient bridge between descriptor learning and metric learning, and construct a Knowledge-Guided Learning Network (KGL-Net), which achieves significant performance improvements while abandoning complex network structures. Specifically, we find that there is feature extraction consistency between metric learning based on feature difference learning and descriptor learning based on Euclidean distance. This provides the foundation for bridge building. To ensure the stability and efficiency of the constructed bridge, on the one hand, we conduct an in-depth exploration of 20 combined network architectures. On the other hand, a feature-guided loss is constructed to achieve mutual guidance of features. In addition, unlike existing methods, we consider that the feature mapping ability of the metric branch should receive more attention. Therefore, a hard negative sample mining for metric learning (HNSM-M) strategy is constructed. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time that hard negative sample mining for metric networks has been implemented and brings significant performance gains. Extensive experimental results show that our KGL-Net achieves SOTA performance in multiple cross-spectral image patch matching datasets. Our code is available at https://github.com/YuChuang1205/KGL-Net

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Can Large Language Models Capture Video Game Engagement?
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2502.04379v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Can out-of-the-box pretrained Large Language Models (LLMs) detect human affect successfully when observing a video? To address this question, for the first time, we evaluate comprehensively the capacity of popular LLMs for successfully predicting continuous affect annotations of videos when prompted by a sequence of text and video frames in a multimodal fashion. In this paper, we test LLMs' ability to correctly label changes of in-game engagement in 80 minutes of annotated videogame footage from 20 first-person shooter games of the GameVibe corpus. We run over 4,800 experiments to investigate the impact of LLM architecture, model size, input modality, prompting strategy, and ground truth processing method on engagement prediction. Our findings suggest that while LLMs rightfully claim human-like performance across multiple domains and able to outperform traditional machine learning baselines, they generally fall behind continuous experience annotations provided by humans. We examine some of the underlying causes for a fluctuating performance across games, highlight the cases where LLMs exceed expectations, and draw a roadmap for the further exploration of automated emotion labelling via LLMs.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SemICP: Semantic Non-Rigid Point Cloud Registration with Elastic Energy Regularization
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2503.00972v5 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Purpose: Accurate point cloud registration is essential in computer-aided interventions (CAI) to align multi-modal medical images for intraoperative guidance. Classical methods, such as Iterative Closest Point (ICP), remain attractive for their explainability and minimal training requirements, but typically ignore anatomical semantics and biomechanical properties during regularization.
  Methods: We present Semantic ICP (SemICP), a novel non-rigid point cloud registration framework that combines semantically informed point matching with linear elastic energy regularization. Semantic labels are used to improve correspondence matching by constraining correspondences to be anatomically consistent. A novel control-point deformation representation with linear-elastic energy regularization is introduced to encourage biomechanically plausible deformations. SemICP was evaluated on a simulation phantom and four datasets against established baselines. It was also tested with labels from AI-based segmentation in a fully automatic segmentation-registration pipeline.
  Results: On the finite element phantom, SemICP recovered 86% of the interior displacement from surface observations alone. On the real datasets, SemICP achieved the lowest target registration error on Liver MR-US and the lowest surface distances on TORS, and ranked second on AbdominalMR-CT and HippocampusMR, where NR-ICP achieved lower surface distances. The fully automatic registration pipeline was shown to be effective for US-MR registration and to improve the alignment of expert-annotated structures.
  Conclusion: SemICP improves interior accuracy at competitive surface accuracy by combining semantic correspondence constraints and linear energy regularization. Combined with AI-based segmentation, SemICP provides an effective pipeline for multi-modal registration in CAI.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: HandReader: Advanced Techniques for Efficient Fingerspelling Recognition
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2505.10267v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Fingerspelling is a significant component of Sign Language (SL), allowing the interpretation of proper names, characterized by fast hand movements during signing. Although previous works on fingerspelling recognition have focused on processing the temporal dimension of videos, there remains room for improving the accuracy of these approaches. This paper introduces HandReader, a group of three architectures designed to address the fingerspelling recognition task. HandReader$_{RGB}$ employs the novel Temporal Shift-Adaptive Module (TSAM) to process RGB features from videos of varying lengths while preserving important sequential information. HandReader$_{KP}$ is built on the proposed Temporal Pose Encoder (TPE) operated on keypoints as tensors. Such keypoints composition in a batch allows the encoder to pass them through 2D and 3D convolution layers, utilizing temporal and spatial information and accumulating keypoints coordinates. We also introduce HandReader_RGB+KP - architecture with a joint encoder to benefit from RGB and keypoint modalities. Each HandReader model possesses distinct advantages and achieves state-of-the-art results on the ChicagoFSWild and ChicagoFSWild+ datasets. Moreover, the models demonstrate high performance on the first open dataset for Russian fingerspelling, Znaki, presented in this paper. The Znaki dataset and HandReader pre-trained models are publicly available.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: FDSG: Forecasting Dynamic Scene Graphs
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2506.01487v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Dynamic scene graph generation extends scene graph generation from images to videos by modeling entity relationships and their temporal evolution. However, existing methods either generate scene graphs from observed frames without explicitly modeling temporal dynamics or predict only relationships while assuming static entity labels and locations. These limitations hinder effective extrapolation of both entity and relationship dynamics, restricting video scene understanding. We propose Forecasting Dynamic Scene Graphs (FDSG), a novel framework that predicts future entity labels, bounding boxes, and relationships, for unobserved frames while also generating scene graphs for observed frames. Our scene graph forecast module leverages query decomposition and neural stochastic differential equations to model entity and relationship dynamics. A temporal aggregation module further refines predictions by integrating observed and forecasted information via cross-attention. To benchmark FDSG, we introduce Scene Graph Forecasting, a new task for full future scene graph prediction. Extensive experiments on Action Genome and VidOR show that FDSG outperforms state-of-the-art methods on dynamic scene graph generation, scene graph anticipation, and scene graph forecasting. Codes will be released upon publication.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Multi-Scale Spectral Attention Module-based Hyperspectral Segmentation in Autonomous Driving Scenarios
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2506.18682v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Recent advances in autonomous driving (AD) have highlighted the potential of hyperspectral imaging (HSI) for enhanced environmental perception, particularly in challenging weather and lighting conditions. However, efficiently processing high-dimensional spectral data remains a significant challenge. This paper presents an empirical investigation of a Multi-Scale Attention Mechanism (MSAM) for enhanced spectral feature extraction through three parallel 1D convolutions with varying kernel sizes (1-11) and adaptive feature aggregation. By integrating MSAM into UNet's skip connections, we evaluate performance improvements in semantic segmentation across multiple HSI datasets for urban driving scenarios. Comprehensive ablation studies demonstrate that MSAM consistently outperforms baseline UNet-SC, achieving average improvements of 2.32% in mIoU and 2.88% in mF1, while maintaining competitive GPU performance against established attention mechanisms. Our findings reveal that optimal kernel combinations are dataset-specific, with configurations such as (1;5;11) and (3;7;11) demonstrating particularly strong performance. This empirical investigation advances understanding of HSI processing capabilities for AD applications and establishes a foundation for adaptive multi-scale spectral feature extraction in automotive deployment.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Autoregressive Image Generation with Linear Complexity: A Spatial-Aware Decay Perspective
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2507.01652v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Autoregressive (AR) models have recently emerged as a promising paradigm for image generation, as they can model visual tokens through the same next-token prediction principle that underlies large language models. However, most competitive AR image generators still rely on Transformer attention, whose quadratic token interaction cost and growing key-value cache become increasingly expensive for high-resolution visual sequences. Linear attention provides an attractive route to efficient AR generation, but our study shows that directly importing linear or decay-based attention from language modeling leads to clear quality degradation. We identify a key cause: after a 2D token map is flattened by raster scan, 1D sequence locality no longer faithfully reflects spatial locality, and conventional decay mechanisms may introduce a false-locality bias at row transitions. To address this problem, we propose Linear Attention with Spatial-Aware Decay (LASAD), a simple recurrent attention mechanism that modulates decay according to the original 2D token geometry while preserving linear complexity. Built upon this layer, LASADGen replaces standard attention in an AR image generator with spatial-aware linear attention. Experiments on ImageNet demonstrate that LASADGen achieves a favorable quality-efficiency tradeoff, improving generation quality over linear-attention baselines while reducing inference cost and memory usage compared with Transformer-based AR models.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Large Language Models for Crash Detection in Video: A Survey of Methods, Datasets, and Challenges
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2507.02074v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Crash detection from video feeds is a critical problem in intelligent transportation systems. Recent developments in large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) have transformed how we process, reason about, and summarize multimodal information. This paper surveys recent methods leveraging LLMs for crash detection from video data. We present a structured taxonomy of fusion strategies, summarize key datasets, analyze model architectures, compare performance benchmarks, and discuss ongoing challenges and opportunities. Our review provides a foundation for future research in this fast-growing intersection of video understanding and foundation models.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Heeding the Inner Voice: Aligning ControlNet Training via Intermediate Features Feedback
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2507.02321v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Despite significant progress in text-to-image diffusion models, achieving precise spatial control over generated outputs remains challenging. One of the popular approaches for this task is ControlNet, which introduces an auxiliary conditioning module into the architecture. To improve alignment of the generation image and control, ControlNet++ proposes a cycle consistency loss to refine correspondence between controls and outputs, but restricts its application to the final denoising steps, while the main structure is introduced at an early stage of generation. To address this issue, we suggest InnerControl -- a training strategy that enforces spatial consistency across a broad range of diffusion steps, including early high-noise ones. Specifically, we train lightweight control prediction probes -- small convolutional networks -- to reconstruct input control signals (e.g., edges, depth) from intermediate diffusion features across denoising steps. We show empirically that such models can extract signals even from very noisy latents and utilize these models to generate pseudo ground truth controls during training. Suggested approach enables alignment loss that minimizes the difference between predicted and target condition over most of the diffusion trajectory. Our experiments demonstrate that our method improves control alignment, with perceptual fidelity preserved or improved in most settings and small FID trade-offs in others. Our approach can be applied to both UNet- and Transformer-based diffusion architectures and be integrated with established training techniques (e.g., ControlNet++) to achieve high performance across different condition methods such as edge, segmentation and depth conditions.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: EAvatar: Expression-Aware Head Avatar Reconstruction with Generative Geometry Priors
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2508.13537v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: High-fidelity head avatar reconstruction plays a crucial role in AR/VR, gaming, and multimedia content creation. Recent advances in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) have demonstrated effectiveness in modeling complex geometry with real-time rendering capability and are now widely used in high-fidelity head avatar reconstruction tasks. However, existing 3DGS-based methods still face significant challenges in capturing fine-grained facial expressions and preserving local texture continuity, especially in highly deformable regions. To mitigate these limitations, we propose a novel 3DGS-based framework termed EAvatar for head reconstruction that is both expression-aware and deformation-aware. Our method introduces a sparse expression control mechanism, where a small number of key Gaussians are used to influence the deformation of their neighboring Gaussians, enabling accurate modeling of local deformations and fine-scale texture transitions. Furthermore, we leverage high-quality 3D priors from pretrained generative models to provide a more reliable facial geometry, offering structural guidance that improves convergence stability and shape accuracy during training. Experimental results demonstrate that our method produces more accurate and visually coherent head reconstructions with improved expression controllability and detail fidelity.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SpecPrune-VLA: Accelerating Vision-Language-Action Models via Action-Aware Self-Speculative Pruning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2509.05614v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Pruning is a typical acceleration technique for compute-bound models by removing computation on unimportant values. Recently, it has been applied to accelerate Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model inference. However, existing acceleration methods focus on local information from the current action step and ignore the global context, leading to >20% success rate drop and limited speedup in some scenarios. In this paper, we point out spatial-temporal consistency in VLA tasks: input images in consecutive steps exhibit high similarity, and propose the key insight that token selection should combine local information with global context of the model. Based on this, we propose SpecPrune-VLA, a training-free, two-level pruning method with heuristic control. (1) Action-level static pruning. We leverage global history and local attention to statically reduce visual tokens per action. (2) Layer-level dynamic pruning. We prune tokens adaptively per layer based on layer-wise importance. (3) Lightweight action-aware controller: We classify actions as coarse- or fine-grained by the speed of the end effector and adjust pruning aggressiveness accordingly. Extensive experiments show that SpecPrune-VLA achieves up to 1.57$\times$ speedup in LIBERO simulation and 1.70$\times$ on real-world tasks, with negligible success rate degradation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Every Camera Effect, Every Time, All at Once: 4D Gaussian Ray Tracing for Physics-based Camera Effect Data Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2509.10759v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Current video diffusion models can generate recognizable camera-effect appearances but do not reliably follow specified physical parameters such as field of view, aperture, and readout time, partly because real dynamic videos with diverse and accurate camera-effect annotations are scarce. Physics-based simulation provides exact labels but suffers from a sim-to-real gap. Reconstructing real dynamic scenes offers an alternative, but Dynamic NeRF methods render too slowly, whereas rasterization-based Dynamic Gaussian Splatting cannot model the light transport required by these effects. We propose 4D Gaussian Ray Tracing (4D-GRT), a two-stage data-generation pipeline that reconstructs dynamic scenes as 4D Gaussians from multi-view pinhole videos and re-renders them with physically based camera models under specified parameters. On CamVFX-4D, our controlled benchmark of eight dynamic indoor scenes under four camera effects, 4D-GRT achieves up to 3.4 dB higher PSNR and 6 times faster rendering than MSTH. Finally, we demonstrate two downstream applications: fine-tuning a video generation model on our data to improve camera-effect control and extending our pipeline to monocular input. Project page: https://shigon255.github.io/4DGRT-project-page/.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Fieldable Low-Light Multi-Task Perception via Foundation-Model-Assisted Domain Adaptation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2509.23626v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Fieldable low-light perception systems require both semantic and geometric scene understanding under severe domain shift and embedded compute constraints. We present FAMDA, a foundation-model-assisted self-training framework for unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) in multi-task dense prediction. The framework integrates segmentation and depth foundation models into a self-training paradigm to generate high-quality pseudo-labels for the target domain, distilling their generalization capabilities into a single lightweight student network. To connect the method to deployment, we instantiate the adapted student on a compact handheld low-light prototype with DomiNite imaging and Jetson Orin Nano embedded compute. We evaluate on standard synthetic-to-real multi-task UDA benchmarks for comparison with prior work and on our field-collected low-light dataset to validate daytime-to-low-light adaptation in the target application setting. Across these evaluations, the proposed approach achieves strong segmentation and depth accuracy with substantially lower memory use and inference latency than direct foundation-model inference, demonstrating a practical path toward embedded multi-task perception for low-light field systems.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Can MLLMs Perceive and Describe Medical Image Quality Beyond Scores?
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2510.01691v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Medical Image Quality Assessment (IQA) serves as a critical safety gate for clinical AI, yet existing approaches rely on scalar metrics that fail to capture the descriptive, expert-like evaluation process central to clinical practice. We introduce MedQ-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark for language-based medical IQA evaluation with MLLMs, establishing a perception--description paradigm across 5 imaging modalities and over 40 quality attributes. The benchmark comprises two complementary tasks: MedQ-Perception probes low-level visual attribute discrimination via 2,600 expert-annotated perceptual queries; MedQ-Description covers both no-reference and comparison description sub-tasks with 708 expert-annotated samples, evaluated through a four-dimensional judging protocol. Comprehensive evaluation of 23 state-of-the-art MLLMs reveals that current models exhibit only preliminary and unstable capabilities, and highlights the urgent need for targeted optimization of MLLMs in medical IQA. Project & Dataset: https://github.com/liujiyaoFDU/MedQ-Bench

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: A-TPT: Angular Diversity Calibration Properties for Test-Time Prompt Tuning of Vision-Language Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2510.26441v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Test-time prompt tuning (TPT) has emerged as a promising technique for adapting large vision-language models (VLMs) to unseen tasks without relying on labeled data. However, the lack of dispersion between textual features can hurt calibration performance, which raises concerns about VLMs' reliability, trustworthiness, and safety. Current TPT approaches primarily focus on improving prompt calibration by either maximizing average textual feature dispersion or enforcing orthogonality constraints to encourage angular separation. However, these methods may not always have optimal angular separation between class-wise textual features, which implies overlooking the critical role of angular diversity. To address this, we propose A-TPT, a novel TPT framework that introduces angular diversity to encourage uniformity in the distribution of normalized textual features induced by corresponding learnable prompts. This uniformity is achieved by maximizing the minimum pairwise angular distance between features on the unit hypersphere. We show that our approach consistently surpasses state-of-the-art TPT methods in reducing the aggregate average calibration error while maintaining comparable accuracy through extensive experiments with various backbones on different datasets. Notably, our approach exhibits superior zero-shot calibration performance on natural distribution shifts and generalizes well to medical datasets. We provide extensive analyses, including theoretical aspects, to establish the grounding of A-TPT. These results highlight the potency of promoting angular diversity to achieve well-dispersed textual features, significantly improving VLM calibration during test-time adaptation. Our code will be made publicly available.
authors: Udaya S. K. P. Miriya Thanthrige

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Vote-in-Context: Turning VLMs into Zero-Shot Rank Fusers
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2511.01617v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In the retrieval domain, candidates' fusion from heterogeneous retrievers is a long-standing challenge, particularly for complex, multi-modal data such as videos. While typical fusion techniques are training-free, they rely solely on rank or score signals, disregarding candidates' representations. This work introduces Vote-in-Context (ViC), a generalized, training-free framework that re-thinks list-wise reranking and fusion as a zero-shot reasoning task for a Vision-Language Model (VLM). The core insight is to serialize both content evidence and retriever metadata directly within the VLM's prompt, allowing the model to adaptively weigh retriever consensus against visual-linguistic content. We demonstrate the generality of this framework by applying it to the challenging domain of cross-modal video retrieval. To this end, we introduce the S-Grid, a compact serialization map that represents each video as an image grid, optionally paired with subtitles to enable list-wise reasoning over video candidates. ViC is evaluated both as a single-list reranker, where it dramatically improves the precision of individual retrievers, and as an ensemble fuser, where it consistently outperforms strong baselines like CombSUM. Across video retrieval benchmarks including ActivityNet and VATEX, the framework establishes new state-of-the-art zero-shot retrieval performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling complex visual and temporal signals alongside text. In zero-shot settings, ViC achieves Recall@1 scores of 87.1% (t2v) / 89.0% (v2t) on MSR-VTT and 99.6% (v2t) on VATEX, representing massive gains of up to +40 Recall@1 over previous state-of-the-art baselines. We present ViC as a simple, reproducible, and highly effective recipe for turning modern VLMs into powerful zero-shot rerankers and fusers. Code and resources are publicly available at: https://github.com/mohammad2012191/ViC

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Transfer the Style, Not the Semantics: Mitigating Semantic Leakage in Image-Guided Stylization
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
arXiv:2511.06365v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Image-guided zero-shot style transfer enables training-free stylization of arbitrary content images using a reference style. Despite recent progress, existing methods commonly rely on self-attention manipulation to inject style information, which may transfer semantic content from the style image, leading to semantic leakage. In this work, we revisit this phenomenon from the perspective of key--value coupling in the self-attention of diffusion models. Our analysis shows that the native correspondence between style keys and values plays an important role in transferring semantic information from the style image. Motivated by this observation, we propose SuRe, a timestep-aware key--value regulation framework that mitigates semantic leakage by disrupting the native key--value correspondence while progressively restoring it for faithful style transfer.
