On ImageNet with $K=16384$, this happens after only about 2 out of 256 positions, when most prefixes already identify individual images in the dataset. We call this phenomenon the Entropy Cliff. Under full conditional utilization, larger codebooks exhaust the finite-data entropy budget in fewer positions. The empirical entropy decreases more gradually in our language comparison, where the effective entropy per position stays below the codebook capacity. To address this, we propose Variable Codebook Size Quantization (VCQ), where the codebook size $K_t$ grows monotonically along the sequence from $K_{\min}=2$ to $K_{\max}$, leaving the loss function, parameter count, and AR training procedure unchanged. With a vanilla autoregressive Transformer and standard next-token prediction, VCQ-Base achieves gFID w/o CFG 14.80 on ImageNet $256\times256$, compared with 27.98 and 18.16 for constant codebooks of size 16384 and 8192, respectively. Scaled up, it reaches gFID 1.71 with 684M autoregressive parameters, without any extra training techniques such as semantic regularization or causal alignment. The extreme information bottleneck at $K_{\min}=2$ encourages semantic concentration in early encoder features: a linear probe on features from only the first 10 positions reaches 43.8% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet, compared to 27.1% for uniform codebooks. These results show that what matters is not only the total capacity of the codebook, but also how that capacity is distributed and organized.

Machine Learning.title: UniSD: Towards a Unified Self-Distillation Framework for Large Language Models
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2605.06597v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Self-distillation (SD) offers a promising path for adapting large language models (LLMs) without relying on stronger external teachers. However, SD in autoregressive LLMs remains challenging because self-generated trajectories are free-form, correctness is task-dependent, and plausible rationales can still provide unstable or unreliable supervision. Existing methods mainly examine isolated design choices, leaving their effectiveness, roles, and interactions unclear. In this paper, we propose UniSD, a unified framework to systematically study self-distillation. UniSD integrates complementary mechanisms that address supervision reliability, representation alignment, and training stability, including multi-teacher agreement, EMA teacher stabilization, token-level contrastive learning, feature matching, and divergence clipping. Across six benchmarks and six models from three model families, UniSD reveals when self-distillation improves over static imitation, which components drive the gains, and how these components interact across tasks. Guided by these insights, we construct UniSDfull, an integrated pipeline that combines complementary components and achieves the strongest overall performance, improving over the base model by +5.4 points and the strongest baseline by +2.8 points. Extensive evaluation highlights self-distillation as a practical and steerable approach for efficient LLM adaptation without stronger external teachers.

Machine Learning.title: Tight Generalization Bounds for Noiseless Inverse Optimization
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2605.08866v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Inverse optimization (IO) seeks to infer the parameters of a decision-maker's objective from observed context--action data. We study noiseless IO, where demonstrations are generated by a ground-truth objective. We provide a high-probability ${O}(\frac{d}{T})$ generalization bound for the induced action set, where $d$ is the number of unknown parameters and $T$ is the size of the training dataset. We strengthen this guarantee under additional conditions that ensure uniqueness of the chosen action, bringing our IO guarantees in line with best-arm identification results in the bandit literature. We further show that the ${O}(\frac{d}{T})$ rate is tight over all consistent estimators considered here, and extend the result to both instantaneous and cumulative regret. Notably, the resulting regret lower bound matches the corresponding upper bounds in the adversarial setting, indicating that the stochastic IO setting is effectively adversarial for the class of estimators studied here. Finally, we propose a parameter-free algorithm with lower per-iteration complexity than generic solvers. Experiments validate the predicted rates and illustrate the tightness of our bounds.

Machine Learning.title: ELF: Embedded Language Flows
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2605.10938v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Diffusion and flow-based models have become the de facto approaches for generating continuous data, e.g., in domains such as images and videos. Their success has attracted growing interest in applying them to language modeling. Unlike their image-domain counterparts, today's leading diffusion language models (DLMs) primarily operate over discrete tokens. In this paper, we show that continuous DLMs can be made effective with minimal adaptation to the discrete domain. We propose Embedded Language Flows (ELF), a class of diffusion models in continuous embedding space based on continuous-time Flow Matching. Unlike existing DLMs, ELF predominantly stays within the continuous embedding space until the final time step, where it maps to discrete tokens using a shared-weight network. This formulation makes it straightforward to adapt established techniques from image-domain diffusion models, e.g., classifier-free guidance (CFG). Experiments show that ELF substantially outperforms leading discrete and continuous DLMs, achieving better generation quality with fewer sampling steps. These results suggest that ELF offers a promising path toward effective continuous DLMs.

Machine Learning.title: Persona-Model Collapse in Emergent Misalignment
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2605.12850v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Fine-tuning large language models on narrow data with harmful content produces broadly misaligned behavior on unrelated prompts, a phenomenon known as emergent misalignment. We propose that emergent misalignment involves persona-model collapse: a deterioration of the internal representations that encode and distinguish personas, undermining the nuance and consistency of their expression. We first test this hypothesis behaviorally, by comparing how models fine-tuned on harmful data and benign controls answer questionnaires while role-playing diverse personas. Across four model families, harmful fine-tuning produces more polarized, all-or-nothing answers, suggesting more binary, less nuanced persona expression. Histograms show increased concentration at the scale endpoints, and Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence quantifies the distributional shift. We also find reduced within-persona consistency: repeated answers to the same question under the same persona become less stable. We reproduce these observations across diverse harmful datasets and questionnaires that probe different aspects of persona-conditioned behavior, while capability and simple instruction-following controls argue against a uniform loss of general ability. Finally, a mechanistic analysis of persona-conditioned activations in Qwen3-235B shows that representations elicited by different persona prompts span fewer effective dimensions in the misaligned variant than in the original and benign-control variants, most clearly in the final layers. Together, these findings provide behavioral and representational support for persona-model collapse as an aspect of emergent misalignment.

Machine Learning.title: Characterizing universal object representations across vision models
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2605.13675v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Deep neural networks trained with different architectures, objectives, and datasets have been reported to converge on similar visual representations. However, what remains unknown is which visual properties models actually converge on and which factors may underlie this convergence. To address this, we decompose the object similarity structure of 162 diverse vision models into a small set of non-negative dimensions. To determine universal versus model-specific dimensions, we then estimate how often each dimension reappears across models. In contrast to model-specific dimensions, universal dimensions are more interpretable and more strongly driven by conceptual image properties, indicating the relevance of interpretability and semantic content as implicit factors driving universality across models. Differences in architecture, objective function, training data, model size, and model performance do not explain the emergence of universal dimensions. However, models with more universal dimensions also better predict macaque IT activity and human similarity judgments, suggesting that universality reflects representations relevant to biological vision. These findings have important implications for understanding the emergent representations underlying deep neural network models and their alignment with biological vision.

Machine Learning.title: Learning Scenario Reduction for Two-Stage Robust Optimization with Discrete Uncertainty
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2605.14494v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Two-Stage Robust Optimization (2RO) with discrete uncertainty is challenging, often rendering exact solutions prohibitive. Scenario reduction alleviates this issue by selecting a small, representative subset of scenarios to enable tractable computation. However, existing methods are largely problem-agnostic, operating solely on the uncertainty set without consulting the feasible region or recourse structure. In this paper, we introduce PRISE, a problem-driven sequential lookahead heuristic that constructs reduced scenario sets by evaluating the marginal impact of each scenario. While PRISE yields high-quality scenario subsets, each selection step requires solving multiple subproblems, making it computationally expensive at scale. To address this, we propose NeurPRISE, a neural surrogate model built on a GNN-Transformer backbone that encodes the per-scenario structure via graph convolution and captures cross-scenario interactions through attention. NeurPRISE is trained via imitation learning with a gain-aware ranking objective, which distills marginal gain information from PRISE into a learned scoring function for scenario ranking and selection. Extensive results on three 2RO problems show that NeurPRISE consistently achieves competitive regret relative to comprehensive methods, maintains strong calability with varying numbers of scenarios, and delivers 17-200x speedup over PRISE. NeurPRISE also exhibits strong zero-shot generalization, effectively handling instances with larger problem scales (up to 5x), more scenarios (up to 4x), and distribution shifts.

Machine Learning.title: Everything at Every Scale: Scale-Invariant Diffusion with Continuous Super-Resolution
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2605.26032v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Creating images from noise is image generation; reconstructing fine details from coarse inputs is super-resolution. Despite their practical differences, both can be understood as reversing information loss across scales. We introduce $\textbf{SKILD}$, a $\textbf{S}$cale-invariant $\textbf{K}$-Space $\textbf{I}$mage $\textbf{L}$earning $\textbf{D}$iffusion model that unifies generation and continuous super-resolution within a single unconditional framework. Both natural images and critical physical systems exhibit scale invariance, and we leverage it to design a forward process that attenuates image content from fine to coarse scales while injecting spectrum-matched Gaussian noise, making scale an explicit coordinate of the diffusion dynamics. The same trained reverse process performs generation and continuous super-resolution by varying only the starting timestep: $\textit{no task-specific architecture, no conditioning branch, no classifier-free guidance, no retraining per scale factor}$. Empirically, SKILD reaches FID $2.61$ and Inception Score $9.65$ on unconditional CIFAR-10, performs $2\times$--$8\times$ super-resolution on ImageNet from a single unconditional checkpoint while outperforming conditional models across perceptual metrics, and reconstructs critical Ising models whose connected four-point correlations closely track the ground truth.

Machine Learning.title: Near-Optimal Decentralized Stochastic Convex Optimization over Networks
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2606.04757v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We study decentralized stochastic smooth convex optimization, where $M$ workers minimize an average objective using local stochastic gradients and neighbor-only communication over a fixed gossip network. A central question in this setting is to determine the largest number of workers that can be used under a total budget of $N$ gradient samples while still preserving the centralized $O(1/\sqrt N)$ statistical rate. We introduce an accelerated decentralized method that preserves this rate for up to $\smash{M\lesssim \sqrt{\rho}\,N^{3/4}}$ workers, where $\rho$ is the spectral gap of the gossip network, improving the best prior maximal scaling of $\smash{M\lesssim \rho\sqrt N}$. The method is based on a one-step-delayed stochastic acceleration scheme that enables workers to interleave minibatching with accelerated gossip while controlling residual disagreement, and its guarantee depends only logarithmically on the optimum-local heterogeneity. We also establish a matching lower bound for linear-span decentralized first-order methods, showing that the method is optimal up to logarithmic factors.

Machine Learning.title: How Far Can Chord-Symbol Time-Series Adaptation Carry Genre Identity? Capabilities and Boundaries in Multi-Genre Chord-Symbol Modeling
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2606.07334v5 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: This report treats chord-symbol sequences as an interpretable, controllable time series for genre-local harmonic modeling. The frozen Music Transformer base is weight-identical to a pop-dominated Phase-0 baseline. I adapt it to eleven target genres: blues, bossa nova, Bach chorales, country, electronic, folk, funk, gospel, hip-hop, R&B/soul, and rock. The main grid compares LoRA, IA3, BitFit, prefix tuning, and full fine-tuning over 11 genres and 3 seeds (165 cells). All five methods improve over the frozen base on held-out chord prediction (macro gains +2.89 to +3.61 percentage points). Top-1 also scores the three header tokens of each sequence, which move whole runs: only a matched adapter predicts its genre marker, and whether a run predicts the placeholder C-major key of every Chordonomicon song is close to arbitrary. Without the header tokens the macro gains are +1.64 to +2.38 pp, and outside Bach chorales LoRA, IA3, prefix tuning, and full fine-tuning give the same gain (+1.30 to +1.34 pp). That gain reflects a handicap of the frozen base, which for every target but rock reads a genre marker it never read in training: given the pop marker instead, it comes within 0.12 pp of the released matched adapter in every non-chorale genre. Wrong-genre adapters beat the frozen base only where it reads such a marker, and outside Bach chorales the matched adapter's edge over the best wrong one is within 0.2 pp. Only on Bach chorales does adaptation add clearly more (+9.6 pp for LoRA over the base given the pop marker). Further diagnostics (rank sweeps, matched-size and same-weights controls, chord-only classification, real songs) support a bounded conclusion: for genres the base already covers, chord-symbol adaptation mainly supplies a usable genre marker, and chord symbols alone do not carry complete genre identity. Perceived genre authenticity is left to controlled listener evaluation.

Machine Learning.title: Querying Counterfactuals on Tissue Graphs with Supervised Disentanglement
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2606.08493v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Tissue graph counterfactuals ask what a cell would express if its spatial neighborhood were altered, a question central to predicting cell behavior in tissues. Existing methods, however, present only specific instances of such queries. In this work, we first formalize tissue graph counterfactuals as a class of spatial interventions that either rewire connections between cells (edge perturbation) or modify the expression of their neighbors (node perturbation). We then introduce Cellina, a framework that uses supervised disentanglement to decompose a cell's intrinsic state from its spatial context, using the latter as a conditioning input for in-silico perturbation predictions. Across benchmarks spanning over 2.5 million spatially-resolved cells in observational and interventional screens, Cellina outperforms both spatially-informed and non-spatial competitors in in-silico perturbations, while training as fast as non-spatial methods. Moreover, we show that Cellina reveals cancer subdomains with distinct signaling programs in an unsupervised manner and enables targeted neighbor perturbation simulations.

Machine Learning.title: Recursively Trained Diffusion Models: Limiting Collapse Distribution and Spectral Characterization
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2606.13796v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Recursive training of generative models on their own outputs can lead to model collapse, a compounding drift away from the true data distribution. Existing theoretical works bound finite-round error accumulation in the context of diffusion models, but two questions remain open:~what distribution does the recursion converge to, and how fast? We answer both, isolating a mechanism distinct from imperfect learning: even with perfect score estimation and exact sampling, the early stopping of the reverse diffusion (required for numerical stability) drives a progressive drift away from the data distribution. We prove that this recursion converges geometrically to a unique limiting distribution, which admits a closed-form characterization as an infinite mixture of increasingly Gaussian-smoothed versions of the data distribution. A Hermite spectral decomposition of this limit reveals that recursive training acts as a low-pass filter: higher-order modes, which encode fine non-Gaussian structure, are attenuated much more strongly than coarse modes. This spectral picture motivates annealed truncation schedules that progressively shrink truncation times across retraining rounds; we prove that any schedule converging to $0$ asymptotically eliminates recursive compounding. Finally, we show our idealized characterization is robust: in the presence of discretization and score estimation errors, the learned distribution remains in a Wasserstein-2 ball around the ideal limit, with mode-dependent contraction rates that contract high-order errors faster than low-order ones. We validate the theory on synthetic Gaussian mixtures and CIFAR-10.

Machine Learning.title: Diffusion-Driven State Space Models
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2606.21036v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: In many domains, practitioners seek models that produce accurate forecasts while faithfully capturing latent system dynamics. Existing approaches typically sacrifice one of these goals: deep state space models often assume Gaussian latent transitions, limiting fit and forecasting, while diffusion models are highly expressive but lack principled inference for the underlying dynamics. To combine the strengths of both, we introduce the Diffusion-Driven State Space Model (DDSSM), which replaces the conventional Gaussian transition distribution with a diffusion model. Our DDSSM resolves the open problem of how to jointly train an autoencoder and a diffusion model on sequential data, thereby extending the literature on latent diffusion models for time series. Moreover, we find that the DDSSM empirically outperforms a state-of-the-art deep SSM at fitting and forecasting a simulated time series with multimodal transitions.

Machine Learning.title: ThermoLLM: LLM-Based Multi-Zone HVAC Control with a Spatiotemporal Context
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2606.22911v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Multi-zone HVAC control is a spatial decision problem in which indoor thermal evolution and control decisions depend not only on outdoor conditions and internal heat gains but also on zone layout, physical adjacency, and delayed thermal interactions across the building. Recent LLM-based HVAC controllers have shown that prompt-based control is feasible. However, these methods produce inconsistent results, are difficult to generalize, and experience control-latency issues. Their performance also relies heavily on numeric reward values, textual feedback, or unstructured retrieval, which limits their ability to make control decisions that account for zone dynamics and thermodynamics. No existing LLM-based methods have used building semantics and dynamics, together with rolling history, as the centre of the LLM context while testing and comparing HVAC control performance with existing LLM-based HVAC approaches. This paper presents ThermoLLM, an LLM-based HVAC control framework tested in a multi-zone building environment. Spatiotemporal context grounding is a main component of ThermoLLM, which uses a spatial knowledge graph derived from Brick-style building semantics and linked with recent observations from a rolling history. We evaluate ThermoLLM against standard control methods and recent state-of-the-art baselines in a five-zone building environment across six climate-season scenarios. ThermoLLM consistently achieves the best energy-comfort trade-offs and outperforms all evaluated baselines in the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) rankings across all six scenarios.

Machine Learning.title: The State-Prediction Separation Hypothesis
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2607.01218v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Transformers use the same forward computation stream to both predict the next token and store useful state for future token predictions. We formulate the state-prediction separation hypothesis: disentangling the two roles yields better language modeling performance. We design a Transformer variant that uses separate computation streams to separate the two functions, and conduct pretraining experiments across various scales. Our experiments show that state-prediction separation consistently offers better data- and compute-efficiency, improving validation loss and outperforming standard Transformers by 2-3 percentage points on average on downstream tasks. We also conduct extensive empirical analysis that rules out potential confounders and demonstrates the fundamental difference in the gradients our design entails.

Machine Learning.title: HyperVAttention: Efficient Sparse Attention with Spatio-Temporal Clustering for Video Diffusion
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2607.03012v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Video Diffusion Transformers (VDiTs) have demonstrated significant capabilities in high-fidelity video generation. However, their ability to produce long-duration videos is fundamentally constrained by the quadratic complexity of the self-attention mechanism. Recent clustering-based sparse attention methods improve the quality-speed trade-off by grouping semantically similar tokens, but their practical efficiency remains limited by two bottlenecks: substantial clustering overhead and low CTA utilization caused by irregular cluster-induced blocks. We propose HyperVAttention (HVA), a training-free sparse attention framework that addresses both bottlenecks jointly. To reduce clustering overhead, we introduce 3D local-window clustering, which exploits the spatio-temporal locality of video tokens to restrict centroid search to fixed local neighborhoods, and implement it with a custom Triton kernel for efficient execution. We further propose a hybrid clustering strategy that performs full clustering only at anchor steps and updates only subset tokens at intermediate steps, leveraging the temporal stability of cluster assignments across denoising steps. To improve CTA utilization, we present hardware-aware cluster merging that minimizes CTA-aligned execution cost through parallel agglomerative merging, improving block density and approximation fidelity by utilizing idle tile capacity. Together, these components reduce clustering overhead, avoid redundant updates, and better align sparse attention with the fixed tile structure of modern GPU kernels. Experiments on video generation show that HVA advances the Pareto frontier of training free sparse attention, achieving higher fidelity than SVG2 at comparable latency and a $2.13\times$ speedup over full attention on HunyuanVideo, or $2.23\times$ with its faster variant HVA-Flash.

Machine Learning.title: Emergent Generalization by Representation Learning in Artificial Neural Networks
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2607.10430v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Dimensionality reduction has proven powerful for identifying neural manifolds, which are low-dimensional structures underlying high-dimensional neural activity. These low-dimensional representations have improved the interpretability of population-level coding. Yet whether such low-dimensional representations are biologically relevant and confer functional advantages in learning systems, or merely reflect neuron-level activity, remains contested in neuroscience. We show that an explicit information bottleneck forcing a recurrent neural network to learn a low-dimensional representation is necessary for rotational and out-of-distribution generalisation in a time-series prediction task. Using information-theoretic measures of causal emergence, we characterise the dynamics of this representation across the memorisation-to-generalisation transition, finding a non-monotonic trajectory which shows an initial decrease, a minimum, and a subsequent rise to a maximum, even as prediction loss falls monotonically. This trajectory scales with task complexity, and the magnitude of emergent structure reliably predicts generalisation performance. Analysis of hippocampal CA1 and medial prefrontal activity in rats learning an alternating maze task reveals analogous non-monotonic emergence dynamics that track behavioural performance. Together, these findings indicate that the ability of neural networks to learn compact, distributed and emergent representations confers a functional advantage for generalisation, supporting a causal role for learned representations in cognition.

Machine Learning.title: Integrating Background Knowledge for Scalable Causal Discovery
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2607.10456v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Expert background knowledge is often available in practical applications of causal discovery. Such constraints on the true causal graph can help causal discovery in terms of identifiability of causal effects and accuracy of the learned structure, but also in reducing the space of candidate causal graphs. As causal discovery can become computationally expensive for large number of variables, it is crucial to utilize background knowledge effectively during the causal discovery process. However, most current methods only use background knowledge in a postprocessing step after causal discovery to refine the learned graph. In this work, we develop a framework for utilizing background knowledge during the causal discovery process, focusing especially on scalable causal discovery methods that recover only a subset of the whole graph. We implement our framework for multiple algorithms and empirically show that utilizing background knowledge can both reduce computational requirements and increase the quality of the learned structures.

Machine Learning.title: Invariant Discovery for Networked Systems
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2607.22944v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Invariants, the relations expected to hold among measured signals of a network, underpin applications from verification to traffic generation, telemetry imputation, and input validation. Yet, writing them by hand demands rare expertise in both formal logic and networking. Testing all possible combinations of telemetry variables statistically is intractable at network scale, while existing automatic tools still require a human-authored grammar of admissible invariants and learn only exact, "hard" rules that break under real-world noise. Our key idea is to use an LLM to inspect variable metadata, classify counter data types, and predict candidate syntactic relationships that form a compact grammar, followed by a deterministic statistical search within that grammar. If the initial grammar fails to recover trusted known invariants on held-out telemetry, Autogram instructs the LLM to iteratively widen the grammar until recovery succeeds. By confining the LLM to grammar induction and re-induction while delegating candidate verification to logical and statistical checks, Autogram turns non-deterministic AI proposals into auditable invariants with formal guarantees within the induced grammar. We design and prototype Autogram and evaluate it on both public and production WAN telemetry, recovering expert-derived invariants with full recall and low false positives. We close with a discussion of open problems on the path toward fully open-ended invariant discovery.

Machine Learning.title: GPTQ-2D: Cubic-Time Two-Sided Adaptive Rounding
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2607.27042v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Adaptive rounding methods such as GPTQ quantize the weights of a large language model (LLM) one at a time, propagating each rounding error to the weights not yet rounded. YAQA lowers the KL divergence from the original model with two-sided adaptive rounding under a Kronecker-factored Hessian, but its error feedback takes quartic work in the size of a square layer. We present GPTQ-2D, which provably computes the same rounding with cubic work, while still rounding the entries of each anti-diagonal in parallel. Its GPU implementation uses two levels of blocking to improve hardware utilization. We also extend the algorithm to Hessians with any number of Kronecker factors. In our experiments, GPTQ-2D is as accurate as YAQA and cuts the time to quantize Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct on a single NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU from 8.6 days to 1.6 hours. Source code is available at https://github.com/IST-DASLab/GPTQ-2D.

Machine Learning.title: Twig: Parallel and Memory-Efficient Tree Speculative Decoding for Hybrid-Attention LLMs
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2608.01651v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Emerging LLMs increasingly interleave full attention with recurrent linear attention to reduce long-context serving costs. Tree speculative decoding could further accelerate these hybrid models, but recurrent linear-attention layers carry parent-dependent states. Existing engines therefore verify proposal trees sequentially and snapshot the full state per node, causing latency and memory to grow with tree and batch sizes. We present Twig, a kernel--runtime co-design for tree speculative decoding of hybrid LLMs. Twig derives a tree-structured factorization of the linear-attention recurrence and realizes it with a resource-efficient GPU kernel that verifies all nodes in parallel, accelerating linear-attention tree verification by 3.4--7.7$\times$. It losslessly represents speculative state updates as token-level factors and reconstructs only the accepted state, reducing transient state memory by 82--99$\times$ and freeing GPU memory for KV caches. We integrate Twig into SGLang, a widely deployed production LLM serving engine, and further optimize its runtime through batch-wide verification budgeting. Across four models, two GPU platforms, and diverse datasets, Twig achieves up to $4.72\times$ the offline decode throughput of autoregressive decoding and up to $2.03\times$ that of the strongest tree-speculative baseline. Under online agent workloads, Twig reduces TTFT and TPOT by up to $67.6\%$ and $49.9\%$, respectively, over the strongest tree-speculative baseline.

Machine Learning.title: Effective pruning of task-trained recurrent neural networks using noisy fluctuations and connection rescaling
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2608.05464v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Pruning network connections is key to brain function but, despite its importance, there exist few biologically-plausible pruning rules with demonstrated good performance. We evaluate noise-prune, a recently introduced unsupervised local pruning rule for recurrent networks that uses noisy fluctuations to determine the importance of connections. Noise-prune has previously only been empirically tested on random networks without a specific computational function. We show that noise-prune preserves task-performance in task-trained recurrent neural networks, greatly outperforming a strategy that only uses connection magnitude and exceeding a non-local strategy that uses second-order information. Rather than deterministically removing connections that fall below a threshold, noise-prune samples connections to preserve based on their importance and strengthens retained connections to preserve average strength. We show that this sampling and rescaling is essential to good performance, and can augment other pruning strategies. We also find that the optimal empirical degree of rescaling is lower than predicted by the original theoretical argument, and thus develop a new version of noise-prune that outperforms the previous version. Our results demonstrate that a biologically-motivated pruning strategy based on local activity statistics can effectively preserve task performance in functional recurrent networks by combining activity-dependent connection selection with compensatory strengthening of surviving connections.

Machine Learning.title: From Siloed Algorithms to Compliance-First Agentic Platforms: A Multi-Layered Architecture for Hospital AI Systems
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2608.06112v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Hospitals are rapidly adopting artificial intelligence for triage, imaging, scheduling etc., yet most deployments remain isolated point solutions locked inside departmental silos, resulting in duplicated effort, hidden risks, and unrealized enterprise value. Despite explosive growth of AI in healthcare market and accelerating investment, an estimated 70-80% of healthcare AI pilots fail to scale, largely due to governance gaps, fragmented data, and missing integration blueprints. This research proposes a hospital-specific, compliance-first, Agentic AI architecture with multiple interoperable layers, extending existing hospital AI platform models with: (i) an Agent Orchestration Layer for multi-agent workflows across clinical, operational, and financial domains, (ii) a Compliance and Policy Layer that centralizes policy-as-code for HIPAA, GDPR, the EU AI Act, DISHA Act, India's DPDP Act, and ISO/IEC security and safety standards, and (iii) a Privacy-Preserving Data Fabric that plugs federated learning, differential privacy, and secure enclaves into real-world Hospital Information Management System (HIMS) flows. Using a synthetic but structurally realistic hospital dataset and an open, ready-to-deploy prototype implementation, this study demonstrates the end-to-end orchestration of triage risk prediction, workflow optimization, and compliance logging, achieving substantial simulated reductions in task turnaround times and manual documentation effort while maintaining policy-guarded data access. The resulting architecture offers hospital leaders a pragmatic blueprint to move from ad hoc tools to a governed, globally compliant, ROI-focused AI platform that can be tailored to on-premise, hybrid and cloud-native deployments.

Machine Learning.title: Population-Scalable Multi-Agent World Modeling across Scene Geometries
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2608.08600v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: World models have recently achieved impressive progress in visual prediction and interactive generation, but extending them to multi-agent environments introduces a fundamental scalability challenge. Existing methods generally assume a fixed number of agents during training and inference, which ties the model to a pre-determined agent population and limits inference-time scalability. Our key insight is that cross-view consistency should arise from a shared world state whose evolution does not assume a predefined number of agents, while agent-specific observations should be generated by querying this state through a unified rendering interface. Based on this insight, we propose Khora, a scalable multi-agent world model that supports inference-time expansion to arbitrary numbers of agents without retraining. Our framework decouples world-state evolution from visual rendering and introduces a population-agnostic rendering mechanism for incorporating other agent information. This design maintains cross-view consistency through the shared world state rather than through dense interactions among observation streams inside the expensive video generator, enabling approximately linear practical scaling with the number of queried views. Qualitative experiments demonstrate that our approach generalizes to unseen numbers of agents while maintaining visual quality and multi-agent consistency. We further implement a real-time interactive system to demonstrate scalable open-world simulation.

Machine Learning.title: GigaBrain-WBC-0.5: A Behavior World Model for Robust Humanoid Whole-Body Tracking with Environment Interaction
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2608.18234v5 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: General-purpose motion trackers enable humanoid robots to follow diverse whole-body motions while maintaining balance, but are trained only on flat ground, failing to exploit bipedal mobility over complex terrain. Cross-terrain controllers, meanwhile, are task-specific or accept only low-dimensional locomotion commands. We introduce InterTrack, the first behavior world model (BWM) for robust whole-body tracking with environment interaction. Its Transformer jointly predicts the next action, state, and behavior distribution, learning environment-conditioned dynamics. To scale interaction training data, an automatic annotation pipeline reconstructs 3D support geometry from retargeted motions. At deployment, the policy handles commands implausible in the current environment in a "best-effort" manner. Quantitatively, InterTrack achieves an 81.3% success rate on terrain interaction (4.3 times the best evaluated baseline) and a 99.3% fall-recovery rate, while also improving free-space tracking and outperforming three leading tracking baselines across all of these regimes. To our knowledge, we provide the first demonstration of real-time cross-terrain whole-body teleoperation on a humanoid robot, alongside object interaction, stable responses to missing supports, and robust recovery from falls.

Machine Learning.title: Inference and Uncertainty Quantification for Streaming $r$-PCA
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2608.18374v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We address two open questions in streaming PCA via Oja's algorithm: sharp operator-norm convergence for general rank under sub-Gaussian data, and distributional inference for the resulting subspace estimator. Existing convergence analyses, even in the rank-one case, either assume bounded data or leave non-vanishing remainder terms that prevent adaptation to a polynomially vanishing tail spectrum, while existing distributional results are confined to the rank-one case. Our convergence theory removes these remainder terms and yields a sharp rate. In the dense-tail spiked covariance regime, this rate matches the minimax rate up to logarithmic factors. More generally, we prove a matching lower bound, up to logarithmic factors, across both dense-tail and sparse-tail regimes under a mild nondegeneracy condition. The analysis yields a linearization of Oja's iterates, which in turn enables a high-dimensional Gaussian approximation for the general-rank subspace estimation error with an explicit limiting covariance. We also establish a row-wise Gaussian approximation over convex sets for the aligned difference, recovering prior rank-one results as special cases. For practical inference, we develop an online multiplier bootstrap algorithm and prove its consistency. Beyond streaming PCA, our techniques contribute to Gaussian approximation and bootstrap inference for nonconvex stochastic approximation.

Machine Learning.title: Speed limits for information acquisition in stochastic learning dynamics
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2609.08219v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Neural networks acquire internal representations through learning. In this work, we formulate stochastic gradient descent (SGD) as a Markovian stochastic process and derive a Fisher-information flow speed limit that bounds the rate at which trainable parameters can acquire information about data-generating parameters. The resulting inequality decomposes the upper bound on the information flow into drift and noise contributions, thereby quantifying the roles of deterministic learning forces and SGD-induced fluctuations from an information-theoretic perspective. We verify the bound in analytically tractable basis-function linear regression, where the information budget predicted by the bound reproduces the ordering and characteristic time scales with which different data-generating parameters are encoded in the learned parameters. These results establish Fisher-information speed limits as a quantitative framework for understanding which properties of the data-generating process are acquired, in what order, and how rapidly they can be encoded in the trainable parameters.

Machine Learning.title: Counterexamples and Sufficient Conditions: Comments on "Optimally-Transported Generalized Method of Moments"
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2609.20260v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We comment on the optimally-transported generalized method of moments (OTGMM) of Schennach and Starck (2026) and give counterexamples to Theorems 2-6. In the small-error analysis, the assumptions do not ensure consistency or asymptotic normality (Theorems 2-3). In the large-error analysis, Theorem 4 states the equivalence between the OTGMM estimator and the GMM estimator with modified moments, and Theorems 5-6 assert consistency and asymptotic normality. Through counterexamples, we show that the equivalence in Theorem 4 fails and a component of the Lagrange multiplier has different limits under the two estimators (Theorems 5-6). We also point out that, under misspecification, the population value selected by OTGMM depends on the metric. We give sufficient conditions and establish results following the original motivation for OTGMM. Our corrections to Theorems 4-6 change their assumptions or interpretation more substantially than those to Theorems 2 and 3. Furthermore, we correct Assumption 16 and the test's null distribution.

Machine Learning.title: PROSWIN: Probabilistic Solar Wind Speed Forecasting Using Deep Distributional Regression From Solar Images
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2609.26683v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Accurately predicting fast solar wind conditions is challenging, as uncertainties are large and unquantified by traditional single-value prediction models. In particular, the risks of high-speed solar wind streams (HSSs), which can cause damage to technological infrastructure, cannot be reliably assessed without probabilistic forecasts. We present PROSWIN, a probabilistic machine learning model that forecasts the hourly solar wind speed (SWS) at Earth with a four-day lead time. The approach combines solar images and magnetograms using a deep neural network coupled to a distributional regression algorithm. Because standard error metrics underweight the relevance of HSS peaks, we further introduce the prediction score, a model-selection metric that jointly rewards timeline and HSS peak accuracy. On 14 years of data, our forecast achieves very well-calibrated uncertainties (<1% average deviation). Using the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), a metric that assesses distributional accuracy, we obtain a timeline CRPS of 41.0 km/s, an HSS peak CRPS of 45.3 km/s, and a prediction score of 42.3 km/s. We find that the 171 {\AA} channel is an important complement to the typically used 193 {\AA} and 211 {\AA} channels and that the prediction score for model selection improves the applicability of the model. Compared to selected models from the literature, ours is the only one that is accurate for both timeline and HSS peak values, rather than trading one off against the other. These results support the advantages of probabilistic over single-value solar wind models. The introduced methods are also transferable to other forecasting problems.

Machine Learning.title: Undertone: Personalizing Frozen VLM Aesthetic Judges from Few Ratings
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2609.27110v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Image quality assessment predicts a mean opinion score (MOS), but for image aesthetics the mean hides the individual, so personalized assessment must start from the few images a new user rates. Fitting each person from scratch fails with ten ratings; networks fine-tuned per person carry over poorly to new kinds of images. We present Undertone-P, which learns from other raters a Gaussian prior over per-person regression weights on read-outs of frozen vision-language model (VLM) judges: the probability-weighted rating and the hidden state at the score token. Since people differ from the crowd in ways other raters reveal, a few ratings need only choose among those ways: a new user costs one closed-form solve, and no network is trained. On Ryu and Yanaka's PARA benchmark, the prior alone reaches a Spearman correlation of .640, above the best published 10- and 100-rating results (.581 and .620); 10 and 100 of a person's ratings raise it to .648 and .676. These ratings add most where tastes depart from the crowd: with 100 ratings, +.067 for the raters who agree least with it and +.206 on LAPIS artworks, against +.037 overall. Without labels, the judges' expected scores predict PARA's MOS at .835 (best published model we ran: .694). PARA-trained networks still lead under PARA's original protocol, likely through a stronger end-to-end MOS model.

Machine Learning.title: Physics-Attested Federated Learning: Securing Collaborative Anomaly Detection in Critical Water Infrastructure
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2609.34804v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Federated learning enables industrial operators to train shared intrusion detection models without disclosing proprietary operational telemetry. However, existing defences operate strictly in update space, leaving aggregators blind to data poisoning; model updates derived from fabricated telemetry remain indistinguishable from honest contributions. We repurpose process invariants, physical relations that always hold in normal operation, such as conservation of mass, from runtime detection heuristics into a verifiable admission requirement for federated updates, mined automatically from clean operational data. We evaluate this admission gate across two physical water testbeds (SWaT, WADI) and a distribution benchmark (BATADAL), testing seven aggregation rules against telemetry fabrication, exposure-only replay poisoning, and an invariant-aware adaptive adversary. Across three testbeds the mined invariants reject none of 25 honest shards except every cross-channel fabrication on SWaT and BATADAL, including optimised perturbations that the similarity based FoolsGold admits in full. On real telemetry, five mined invariants detect 12 of SWaT's 35 attacks, while nine invariants detect 20. With nine invariants, the admission gate removes 78% of the targeted-attack recall lost to replay poisoning (95% CI 57--97%, $p < 0.001$ over 20 seeds) across five standard aggregators, and 82% under FedAvg. To reconcile physical admission control with federated data privacy, we show invariant compliance using zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs) to allow clients to prove batch adherence without revealing operational telemetry.

Machine Learning.title: Backdoor Containment via Expert Quarantine and Shutdown in LLMs
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2610.00663v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Backdoored large language models (LLMs) can behave normally on benign inputs while producing attacker-specified outputs under hidden triggers. Existing defenses span four stages---prior-training, in-training, post-training, and inference-time---and share one of two underlying strategies: either suppress backdoor learning (by filtering poisoned data or interrupting its acquisition during optimization) or learn, then purify (by repairing model weights or gating inputs after a fully backdoored model has formed). We propose a third strategy, learn, but channel: allow backdoor formation during training but route it into a designated, quarantined component that can be disabled at deployment. To this end, we propose Quarantined Expert Shutdown QES, a computationally efficient containment strategy built in a regularization-steered MoE-like setting. Specifically, given a poisoned dataset, QES augments a Transformer-based language model with routed expert-specific LoRA branches and lightweight routers, and uses auxiliary routing objectives to attract trigger-conditioned behavior into a designated expert while preserving benign capability elsewhere. At deployment, mitigation reduces to a single constant-time operation: zeroing the quarantined expert's routing weight, without trigger screening or further updating model weights. Empirically, our methods reduce the attack success rate (ASR) from 100% to 0-10% on most settings across two tasks, three attacks, and four model families, while downstream utility is often preserved or only modestly affected. These results establish learn, but channel as a previously unexplored regime for backdoor containment in generative LLMs.

Machine Learning.title: Backdoor Purification for LoRA-Tuned LLMs via Null-Space Projection
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2610.00685v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: With the rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods, the risk of backdoor attacks has become more severe. Existing backdoor purification methods typically rely on at least one of the strong assumptions, such as prior knowledge of triggers, access to clean references, or aggressive retraining, and they often lack comprehensive evaluations. These constraints substantially limit their practical applicability. To overcome these challenges, our work proposes purifying LoRA-tuned LLMs without these assumptions and even without post-hoc retraining of the suspect parameters. Our objective is to significantly reduce the attack success rates (ASR) while preserving both (i) the base model's general capabilities and (ii) the new downstream skills learned through the adapter. Through a series of examinations, we progressively scale our approach from a single layer in a text classification setting to a full-parameter LLM in the generative task. Through careful data curation and feature approximation, we extract high-fidelity backdoor directions and, for each layer or head, construct orthogonal null spaces in both the input and output channels, onto which the LoRA updates are projected. Empirically, our null-space projection method reduces the ASR from nearly 100% to less than 10%, while preserving the base model's benign performance and the adapter's learned abilities during downstream task adaptation.

Machine Learning.title: VIGOR: Zero-Shot Visual Generalization via Latent-Space Consistency in Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2610.02801v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) achieves strong sample efficiency by planning in learned latent dynamics but degrades substantially under unseen visual distractions such as background, lighting, or camera changes. Unlike model-free RL, where encoder perturbations affect only single-step predictions, MBRL suffers from a two-level vulnerability: distractions push encoder outputs out of distribution, and these errors compound through recursive latent rollouts. We propose visual generalization via latent-space consistency in model-based RL (VIGOR), which enables zero-shot generalization to unseen distractions while retaining its backbone's sample efficiency. VIGOR comprises three interdependent components: (i) asymmetric weak-to-strong augmentation, which pairs weak-only and weak-to-strong latent views within a batch; (ii) dynamics-level consistency, which enforces augmentation-invariant transition predictions via direct latent regression; and (iii) encoder-level stabilization, which prevents encoder drift under the cross-augmentation supervision of (ii). On the DeepMind Control Suite (DMC) and Robosuite, VIGOR instantiated on TD-MPC2 outperforms state-of-the-art model-free and model-based baselines in zero-shot generalization, surpassing the second-best baseline by 3.4% on DMC and 43.6% on Robosuite, with sample efficiency comparable to its backbone and fewer environment interactions than the other baselines. Ablations show that VIGOR is augmentation-agnostic: augmentations from distinct perturbation families preserve strong generalization, confirming that latent-space consistency, not the augmentation choice, drives robustness. A second instantiation on DreamerV3, a structurally distinct recurrent state-space model, also improves zero-shot generalization on both benchmarks, indicating backbone-agnostic benefits. Code and videos: https://vigor-gen.github.io/.

Machine Learning.title: Structural and Representational Agency in LLM-Driven Timbre Generation and Interpolation
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2610.12532v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Generative creative interfaces routinely report the user's position within a space of possibilities. Such displays imply that the quantities shown were measured from the artefact; in a growing class of systems they are instead predicted by a language model describing its own output, and the two are indistinguishable on screen. Most creative domains lack an agreed measurement against which such a self-report can be checked; audio admits one. In a measurement study of a working LLM-driven timbre interface, what a user can cause proves separable from what the interface reports. The first is exactly characterisable: the reachable set is a zonotope in parameter space whose dimension increases by one per sound placed, so the space the model may act within is demonstrably the user's own. The second is inaccurate. The displayed position differs from measurement by approximately three times the width of that region, and the error has two independent sources: model-predicted coordinates, whose accuracy varies twofold between the two models evaluated, and the interpolation step, which arises from combining synthesiser parameters and is unaffected by model quality. End to end, 27 of 36 refinement instructions produced no perceptible change, and under the weaker model the facility performed no action while reporting convergence. Effective agency (what a user can cause) and epistemic agency (whether they can know it) are therefore separable and independently engineered: structurally enforced constraints survive model failure, whereas guarantees resting on the model's own report do not. The failure mode that remains is silence presented as success. We close with a short protocol for building and auditing such displays.

Machine Learning.title: Beyond Equation Search: Conjecture-Guided Discovery with SCOPE and ClosureBench
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2610.18938v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Most symbolic regression methods optimize candidate equations, but improving an equation's fit does not establish whether its underlying scientific conjecture should be retained, revised, or rejected. A conjecture may admit multiple mathematical realizations, and similarly accurate equations may imply different explanations. This motivates a shift from refining individual expressions to developing and testing the conjectures that guide them. We introduce SCOPE, a framework that sustains multiple conjecture-driven research trajectories. Multiple scientist agents independently pursue conjectures through equation modeling, question formulation, and active experimentation, then exchange evidence to revise their conjectures and research directions. Their findings are consolidated into a scientific report linking models, conclusions, and evidence. Existing equation-discovery benchmarks primarily assess recovered expressions, leaving the evidence and scientific conclusions established through the investigation underexamined. We therefore introduce ClosureBench, an interactive benchmark of 60 closure-discovery tasks across five scientific domains. ClosureBench focuses on closure-discovery tasks to give equation discovery a concrete scientific purpose. Each task embeds an unknown algebraic relation in a known PDE system, where agents control experimental conditions in OpenFOAM to acquire new data for equation discovery. Beyond equation accuracy, ClosureBench proposes three metrics to evaluate the discovery process: evidence faithfulness, mechanism insight, and experimental effectiveness. Compared with diverse baselines, SCOPE achieves higher equation accuracy on both ClosureBench and a real-world scientific discovery case, while producing more accurate, reliable, and effective scientific discoveries.

Machine Learning.title: Revisiting Generative vs. Dense Retrieval: A Static Value Prior Reverses the Gap
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2610.19065v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Generative retrieval (GR) has emerged as a strong candidate generator for sequential recommendation as language models and semantic-item identifiers have improved. However, GR is not a uniformly stronger replacement of dense retrieval (DR) in online retail candidate generation. We examine their differences on two Amazon Toys datasets under different metrics. GR leads on best relevant item value among users both methods cover, while DR leads on exact-target recall and relevant value across the ranked list. With deep analysis, we find that popularity contributes the most to GR's measured value lead. Adding the same static item value to DR in one reranking step reverses this lead and keeps recall above GR. Finally, on an industrial-scale internal e-commerce dataset with LLM-judged relevance, we show that a 14B SID-LLM still underperforms a $47\times$ smaller dense encoder.

Machine Learning.title: Privacy-Preserving Text Inference for Health-Misinformation Classification and Semantic Retrieval
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2610.20796v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Health-misinformation analysis presents a dual challenge: misleading claims can affect public well-being, while systems designed to detect them may expose sensitive user-submitted text. This motivates privacy-preserving inference for public-health applications in which user queries may contain confidential medical information and trained models and reference databases are maintained on organizational servers. We design a privacy-preserving text inference framework based on CKKS homomorphic encryption for health-misinformation classification and semantic retrieval. The classification pipeline fuses BioBERT embeddings, PCA-reduced MPNet embeddings, and SVD-reduced TF-IDF features, while the retrieval pipeline combines MPNet embeddings with ISCC-SCT semantic fingerprints through late fusion. We evaluate predictive performance and benchmark plaintext versus ciphertext-based execution. The hybrid classifier achieved an accuracy of 0.971 and a macro-F1 score of 0.950, with identical reported metrics under plaintext and ciphertext-based inference. The hybrid late-fusion similarity model achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.8691 with human sentence-pair similarity scores on STS-B. For ciphertext-based retrieval, we evaluated naive and optimized implementations. The optimized implementation uses CKKS single instruction, multiple data (SIMD) packing to compute and return multiple similarity scores together, reducing single-query latency over 7,128 indexed items from 222.028 to 5.168 seconds and communication overhead from 6.11 GB to 2.13 MB. These findings demonstrate the technical feasibility of privacy-preserving text inference for health-misinformation applications and characterize its predictive utility and efficiency trade-offs.

Machine Learning.title: Single-stage joint diffusion of sky images and clear-sky index for ultra-short-term irradiance forecasting: what the frame-to-irradiance stage discards
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2610.21795v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Sky-image irradiance forecasting is dominated by a two-stage design: a video-prediction model forecasts future sky frames, and a separately trained regressor maps those frames to irradiance. We propose a single-stage alternative that co-denoises the future sky-image and clear-sky-index sequences in one diffusion process, with an irradiance head that reads a denoised preview of the future sky rather than the noised diffusion state. The forecaster needs no regression stage and runs from sky images and deterministic covariates alone, with no measured irradiance at its input --- the situation at a site with a camera but no pyranometer. On 2023 SIRTA data the model reaches a pooled RMSE of $104.1$~W\,m$^{-2}$ and a skill score of $+0.34$ on the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) against smart persistence, higher than any of twelve baseline configurations, and retains that skill when retrained on 2021--2022. On the model's own generated frames, a separately trained regressor reaches $150.6$~W\,m$^{-2}$ against the joint head's $104.1$: roughly $46$~W\,m$^{-2}$ that joint training recovers and a cascade discards. Point accuracy is competitive but not best: a deterministic network that also reads measured irradiance attains $97.6$~W\,m$^{-2}$. The model's CRPS skill leads that network's in every sky-condition tertile, by $0.26$ to $0.30$.

Machine Learning.title: No Escape from the Quadratic Barrier: Adaptive Attacks on Linear $\ell_2$ Sketches
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2610.25008v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Linear sketches estimate properties of high-dimensional inputs from a fixed low-dimensional projection. At constant accuracy, randomized Euclidean-norm sketches, notably the Johnson-Lindenstrauss transform, support exponentially many nonadaptive queries in sketch dimension $k$. For adaptive black-box queries, known privacy-based defenses guarantee $\widetilde{\Omega}(k^2)$ and it remained open whether stronger guarantees were possible. Prior attacks used more queries, restricted the responder, or provided weaker failure guarantees. We show that the quadratic guarantee is optimal up to logarithmic factors, even with a computationally unbounded responder that knows the matrix, attack algorithm, history, and query distributions and may change its randomized rule after every query. For every fixed hidden $A\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times n}$ with $n>40k$ and target accuracy $\alpha \in (0,1]$, our black-box attack uses $O(k+\alpha^2k^2\log(2+\alpha^2k))$ queries in $\widetilde{O}(1+\alpha^2k)$ adaptive rounds to force, with constant probability, a round in which a constant fraction of answers have $\Omega(\alpha)$ relative error. This fraction can be taken arbitrarily close to one half. Our results clarify the limits of defending a fixed compressive linear representation by adapting the prediction rule.

Machine Learning.title: Memory before Goal: Role of Pre-History Memory for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2610.31166v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation in dynamic scenes is non-Markovian: cues vanish as objects change or are hidden, or leave the view as the robot turns and walks, yet whole-body vision-language-action (VLA) policies see only the present. We present WholeBodyMem, an object-guided perceptual memory that keeps the pre-history of object events seen before the robot acts on its goal. SAM3 tracks the task objects, and their events causally select key frames within an adaptive budget, which the action expert reads by cross-attention together with object tokens encoding appearance, geometry and time. We also contribute HuMeGo, a humanoid memory benchmark with six simulated and six real-world Unitree G1 tasks. Keeping the right frames rather than more frames, WholeBodyMem surpasses memoryless and uniform-memory baselines, raising its base policy's success from 29.1% to 72.6% in simulation and from 36.7% to 88.3% on the real robot, while also improving the standard SIMPLE tasks (70.2% to 86.9%).

Machine Learning.title: Global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ Convergence of Multilevel Gradient-Regularized Newton Methods
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2610.35195v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We develop and analyze multilevel gradient-regularized Newton methods for unconstrained convex optimization with Lipschitz-continuous Hessians. By computing Newton corrections in lower-dimensional subspaces, the proposed methods aim to reduce computational costs while preserving the global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ convergence rate in function values of the full-space method. To establish this rate for multilevel methods, we introduce a class of row-nested restriction operators that ensures monotonicity of the reduced-gradient norms across levels. Numerical experiments with row-nested operators demonstrate convergence behavior comparable to full-space gradient-regularized Newton, while offering substantial computational savings on large-scale instances.

Machine Learning.title: TSBPO: Tree-Structured Branching for Policy Optimization in Interactive Language Agents
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2610.41697v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Terminal feedback in multi-turn agent training leaves both rollout allocation and local credit underdetermined. Dynamics-Predictive Sampling (DPS) [9] provides a task-level predictive sampling reference, but interactive agents also need to choose which visited states merit further continuations. We introduce TSBPO with two method components. A lightweight, fine-grained Root/Branch budget allocator distributes factual rollouts across tasks and additional suffixes across replayable states using likelihood-fitted estimates of terminal-outcome contrast. On the resulting physical rollout trees, a tree-aware step-level credit assignment algorithm compares immediate sibling segments and assigns their local outcome contrasts to the turns they contain. Exact task/observation groups provide a complementary step term. The allocator selects what to sample; observed outcomes determine the subsequent credit. With a Qwen2.5-1.5B actor, fixed checkpoints attain 97.79% seen and 96.64% unseen stochastic success on ALFWorld, and an 81.07% per-episode success rate over six stochastic episodes for each of the 500 WebShop test goals. At the WebShop update-100 checkpoint, removing the observation-group step term yields 75.93% under the same evaluation. These results describe the evaluated training configurations on two interactive benchmarks.

Machine Learning.title: Sampling Design and Confidence Tubes for Integral Curves on Riemannian Manifolds
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2611.00771v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We estimate the integral curve of an unknown vector field from noisy tangent vector field on a known compact Riemannian manifold. We consider two sampling settings: independent observations at random locations that have already been collected, and a fixed response budget that allows subsequent locations to be chosen using pilot information. Under suitable regularity assumptions, the passive kernel estimator has curve error of order $n^{-2/(d+3)}$ in probability, with sample size $n$ and manifold dimension $d$. Its functional central limit theorem has a limit characterized by a linear stochastic differential equation. For active sampling, an independent pilot directs one new batch of measurements to neighborhoods of the target curve. Under localization, smoothness and design conditions, this concentration yields expected maximum curve error of order $N^{-1/2}$, including the pilot in the total response budget $N$. Both methods provide simultaneous geodesic confidence tubes with asymptotically exact coverage under mild conditions. Simulations show narrower active tubes in most reported settings, with improved small-sample coverage in some three-dimensional examples. Ocean-drifter observations illustrate mean-flow reconstruction on the sphere, and a canopy-flow LDA application uses retrospective active sampling to quantify lateral and vertical departures of local mean streamlines.

Machine Learning.title: Write Facts the Way Models Read Them: Lifting the Two-Hop Curse
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2611.01519v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: A language model that learns a new fact by fine-tuning can repeat it but cannot reason with it: taught that a person is a citizen of a new country, it still cannot say, without chain-of-thought, who the head of state of that person's country is. This two-hop curse is widely treated as a reasoning deficit, and the strongest knowledge editors answer it with synthesized reasoning data. We show that the reasoning is intact and the writing is wrong. Fine-tuning writes a new fact as an answer to be said, whereas the second hop reads the bridge ("that person's country") as an entity, from the middle layers on: patching the model's own representation of the entity into the bridge at those layers largely restores the second hop, yet after fine-tuning the bridge there is no closer to the new entity than before the edit. We therefore propose read-equivalent writing (Legible): one loss term makes the bridge phrase, at the layer where the second hop finishes reading it, match the model's own reading of the new entity, and keeps the same relation's other subjects unchanged. Phrases and targets come from the edited model itself, and no multi-hop training data is used. Across Qwen2.5, Llama-3 and Qwen3, Legible (I) composes learned facts more often than the model composes its own knowledge, on MQuAKE's two-hop-curse questions; (II) reaches 1.8-2.6x the bridge accuracy of CaKE, whose reasoning data composes no better than plain fine-tuning, and has the best average over composition, accuracy and locality against four families of writers; and (III) lifts the curse on RippleEdits, on the benchmark of Balesni et al., who named the curse, and at 14B.

Machine Learning.title: Seeing Why: Exact Evidence Maps for Quantum and Optical Image Classifiers
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2611.01993v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: When an image classifier decides, we can usually only estimate why. For quantum and all-optical classifiers that act linearly on amplitude-encoded pictures up to the measurement, with no trained classical network before or after them, each class's Born probability above its no-information share, $P_g - b_g$, splits exactly into contributions of the encoded amplitudes, shown as Born evidence maps (BEM). The split itself follows from known results on quadratic forms: with the transmitted light held fixed, it is what Integrated Gradients from a zero baseline and the Shapley value give. What we add is a way to measure it on the hardware that classifies, from class probabilities on a quantum chip or, in simulation, from camera frames on a lens bench, with no gradient circuit and no light sent backwards; a $g\times g$ map takes $1 + 2g^2$ runs. Deleting the 5% of pixels with the highest evidence drops accuracy from 73% to 9% (one seed), as occlusion and gradient $\times$ input do, while plain gradients remove much less. The classifiers share one architecture, a Fourier-plane mask followed by a brickwall circuit on qubits or by phase plates on a lens bench, read by a fixed Born headroom readout with no trained parameter; centring each picture on its own mean lets dark features count as much as bright ones. In simulation, four phase plates at one wavelength reach 72.3% on Caltech-10 colour photographs. On IBM's ibm_kingston, with the mask computed classically before approximate loading, 300 test pictures were classified at 37.7% against 10% chance (56.3% in exact simulation), and $2\times2$ maps of the filtered input of 30 test pictures drawn at random in advance, measured on the chip, agreed with the exact ones ($r = 0.88$; standard estimator 0.82). The maps also revealed a shortcut in the data; as the trim that removed it was chosen on test pictures, the Caltech-10 results are exploratory.

Machine Learning.title: Distinguishing Initial-Condition and Model Error Using Machine-Learning Weather Models
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2611.05592v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Differentiable weather models allow atmospheric initial conditions to be directly optimized to shadow a known trajectory, which we take from a reanalysis dataset. Here, we extend this optimization to include the forecast model, GraphCast, using low-rank adaptation (LoRA). We compare model optimization with initial-condition (IC) optimization, and then joint optimization, where both are tuned simultaneously. When compared against a control forecast initialized with reanalysis data, LoRA and IC optimization individually produce similar improvements. We find similar results when IC and LoRA are jointly optimized across a spectrum of solutions where a tuning coefficient smoothly shifts the weight of the joint optimization from all-LoRA to all-IC; forecast improvement is not unique to the relative contributions of model and IC corrections. To better discriminate the source of error, we introduce a second model, Pangu-Weather, as a supervisor that gates IC updates during joint optimization. This gated optimization is the same as before, except that IC updates at each epoch are accepted only when they improve the forecasts of both models; otherwise, only the LoRA update is accepted. Results show that this cross-model constraint substantially improves agreement between the two models in their response to the same optimized ICs, narrowing the gap in mean forecast error reduction from 64% to 10%. Moreover, when used together, the LoRA and IC corrections from the gated optimization yield GraphCast forecast improvements similar to those from the ungated optimization. These results imply that model error that is encoded in the ungated ICs is shifted to the LoRA corrections via gating, yielding IC corrections that may provide better analysis estimates.

Machine Learning.title: ZipDrift: Generating Multimodal Short-Horizon MPC Costs with One-Step Drifting Models
Machine Learning.summary:
arXiv:2611.05793v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Short-horizon model predictive control (MPC) is fast but myopic. ZipMPC compensates by learning a context-dependent correction of the short-horizon cost that imitates a long-horizon expert. We observe that the optimal correction is often multimodal: when a slower opponent can be passed on either side, good corrections of opposite sign coexist, and the expert's choice between them hinges on tiny cost differences. Deterministic regression then averages modes or inherits inconsistent expert tie-breaking. We propose ZipDrift, which trains a one-step drifting generator over MPC cost corrections, tilted toward low closed-loop cost and learned only from cost evaluations of candidate corrections, without differentiating through the optimiser. A few generated candidates are ranked by a learned critic, and the model-based MPC then enforces dynamics and constraints. In a kinematic overtaking benchmark derived from ZipMPC, more than half of the contexts are bimodal and the manual short-horizon MPC crashes in 28% of them. With an eight-dimensional stagewise correction, evaluated on 1000 fresh contexts and five training seeds, ZipDrift with eight candidates crashes in 0.74% of episodes, compared with 3.4% for an idealised ZipMPC-style regressor and 2.1% for critic-ranked random candidates with the same budget. A mixture density network (MDN) with the same selection is equally good (0.76%). The benefit of drifting lies in sample quality: in a pre-specified test on further unseen contexts, a single drifting sample crashes in 8.7% of episodes against 13.2% for the MDN, and ZipDrift needs four candidates instead of eight to fall below 1%. With many candidates, all methods degrade as selection exploits errors of the critic.

Multimedia.title: DiaHeads: Jointly Generating Coordinated 3D Dialogue Heads with Non-verbal Cues from Dual Audio
Multimedia.summary:
arXiv:2611.06970v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio-driven 3D head animation has made considerable progress in generation realism, yet generating coordinated behavior for two-person dialogue remains difficult, because current dialogue head generation methods overlook the modeling of non-verbal behavior semantics between the two participants. To address this limitation, we present DiaHeads, a framework that generates the behavior of both participants jointly. The two audio streams are concatenated and decoded together, so each participant's motion is conditioned on the other, which makes the interaction part of the generation itself. We further introduce four discrete non-verbal cues, gaze-on, head shaking, nodding, and smiling, and fuse them with the continuous parameters in a shared latent space through a product-of-experts posterior. These cues carry the interaction semantics and constrain how the continuous motion is generated. A flow-based prior over the shared latent variable replaces the standard Gaussian prior and makes the latent motion temporally dependent. These designs therefore yield coordinated 3D dialogue heads. To support this task we build CANDOR-FG, a dialogue corpus derived from CANDOR and augmented with synchronized FLAME parameters and 3D gaze for both interlocutors. Experiments on CANDOR-FG show that DiaHeads achieves competitive per-participant fidelity and substantial gains in interpersonal coordination over single-speaker and dyadic baselines. In addition, ablations confirm that joint generation, the flow-based prior, and multi-cue supervision are the sources of this coordination. Finally, a user study shows that the advantage of DiaHeads comes from perceived interactional coordination rather than from raw motion fidelity alone.

Multimedia.title: EDGAR: Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement via Synthetic Failure
Multimedia.summary:
arXiv:2611.07909v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Recent advances in Gaussian splatting have enabled efficient and photorealistic head avatar reconstruction, yet monocular video-based or image-based methods still suffer from under-constrained geometry and texture, leading to artifacts such as blurring, stretching, and temporal instability.
